#1838. Manchester United 3-2 Roma: Matheus Cunha the hero as pressure eases on Michael Carrick

Matheus Cunha’s late brace secured Manchester United a jaw-dropping 3-2 comeback win against Roma to breathe new life into their season and ease some of the pressure on Michael Carrick.

A nine-match winless run had left the Red Devils head coach’s job hanging by a thread and Tuesday’s wretched start in the Champions League only pushed him closer to the Old Trafford exit.

United were facing a fourth straight loss after Matias Soule’s avoidable opener was followed up by a Donyell Malen penalty in a first half that ended with boos.

Green and gold balloons had cascaded down the Stretford End as fans protested against owners the Glazer family before the match, with the second half offering a reminder of the special spirit that underpins their club.

Bruno Fernandes pulled one back from a retaken, and softly awarded, spot-kick as United played with the kind of purpose and skill lacking this term.

That approach forced a late error that Cunha capitalised on, before the Brazil forward slammed in off the inside of the near post for the winner.

His celebration earned him the first of two quick bookings but the relief was as palpable as the delight as United held on for just their third win of the campaign.

What ended up being a famous European night under the Old Trafford light had started in frustrating, and all too familiar, fashion.

United shot themselves in the foot against the absentee-hit visitors inside 11 minutes as Roma capitalised on a gaping hole left by left-back Diogo Dalot committing forward. Rodrigo Mora’s diagonal pass was just too high for Ayden Heaven – in for the out-of-sorts Lisandro Martinez – and Soule continued unmarshalled to slam home.

More shambolic defending gifted Roma a quickfire second. Dalot’s positioning again saw the hosts wobble and Heaven was adjudged to have handled a fizzing shot. Referee Jesus Gil Manzano pointed to the spot and former Aston Villa forward Malen converted.

United survived a scare shortly after as Dalot’s difficult night continued before tennis balls landed on the pitch as the clock hit 20 minutes and five seconds – a nod to the Glazers’ leveraged buyout in 2005.

Malen forced a save from Senne Lammens and Soule struck narrowly wide in stoppage time, just after Kobbie Mainoo had the home side’s first shot on target, with home fans fuming at the break.

Cunha was adjudged to have been fouled and fired the ball into the crowd in a bid to liven them up, only for Fernandes’ penalty to be stopped by third-choice goalkeeper Devis Vasquez.

But Bryan Cristante had encroached before clearing the loose ball and the United skipper made no mistake with his thumping second attempt in the 58th minute.

An equaliser nearly followed as Cunha slipped Bryan Mbeumo behind but the forward’s strike hit both posts.

Roma looked shellshocked by United’s newfound intensity. Harry Maguire saw a header blocked from a corner and another led to a Dalot attempt being cleared off the line.

A smattering of boos welcomed Martinez’s introduction along with popular homegrown talent Shea Lacey, who felt he should have been awarded a penalty.

United kept pushing and levelled in the 83rd minute when Leonardo Balerdi misread the bounce on a clipped Fernandes cross, with Cunha taking a touch to finish from close range.

There was fight and belief around the ground and in the 86th minute, Lacey’s pass inside to Cunha was met by a touch and thumping effort off the inside of the near post, sparking wild scenes around Old Trafford.

Cunha earned a booking for celebrating shirtless in the crowd and collected another for a late challenge, but it mattered not as United held on for victory.

#1837. Thierry Henry makes Arsenal comparison in new Manchester United verdict

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Thierry Henry has likened Manchester United’s recent plight to Arsenal’s in the post-Arsene Wenger era.

Before the Red Devils faced Roma in the Champions League, they were coming off a nine-game winless run that saw Michael Carrick mightily close to the sack after a torrid stretch of results that saw United 17th in the Premier League table and 20th in Europe’s premier competition.

They were without a victory since late August, registering just two maximum-point returns all season, against Ipswich Town and minnows Sabah.

Arsenal legend Henry compared United’s current situation to that of his former club when the Gunners were looking to rebuild in Wenger’s final years, through Unai Emery and now Mikel Arteta, who has led the north Londoners to a first top-flight title in 22 years.

“If you go back to the last years of Arsene Wenger, Unai Emery and the beginning of Mikel Arteta, it was a tiny bit toxic,” Henry said on CBS.

“The fans were going amongst each other, asking who the coach should be, who should come and go, having a go at the owners.

“It’s a bit like what’s happening with United now. Surely, along the way, all the coaches they’ve had could have been the answer? Did they give enough time to that one, you don’t know who it could have been? You have guys that are strict, not strict, experienced, not experienced, club legends... it didn’t work.

“You’re telling me that none of those coaches could have turned it around? Were they given time to turn it around? Arteta at times didn’t have great runs in the league; didn’t finish where Arsenal are supposed to finish. They kept him.

“Now everyone is saying he’s a great coach. If he didn’t have the time to show that he was a good coach, we would have said that he was inexperienced, couldn’t handle it and couldn’t win.”

Carrick oversaw a 3-2 win against Roma on Tuesday in a dramatic comeback at Old Trafford that had threatened to turn toxic once more as United fell 2-0 down inside 18 minutes against the in-form Italians.

They roared back in the second period to claim all three points, in a result that will give their under-fire boss more time as they prepare to face Aston Villa at home this weekend.

#1836. West Ham sack Nuno Espirito Santo, "temporary" replacements named ahead of Cardiff City fixture

By Darren Plant | 03 Nov 2026 09:44

West Ham United have announced that they have sacked head coach Nuno Espirito Santo.

When the Hammers were sitting at the top of the Championship table after thrashing Wrexham on September 11, the Portuguese appeared in line to spearhead the club's promotion bid.

However, West Ham have won just two of their last six games in the second tier, one of which came against a Lincoln City outfit who had been quickly reduced to 10 men.

In the two matches since the East Londoners defeated then-leaders Swansea City in South Wales, they suffered home defeats to Southampton and West Bromwich Albion respectively.

Despite West Ham facing Cardiff City on Wednesday night, the club's board have decided to part ways with Nuno.

A statement read: "West Ham United can confirm that men’s first-team Head Coach Nuno Espírito Santo has left his position with immediate effect.

"Following a thorough review of the start to the EFL Championship season, the Board of Directors believe that a change is necessary at this time in order to ensure that the Club’s objectives and expectations remain on track.

"Assistant Head Coach Rui Pedro Silva and Goalkeeper Coach Rui Barbosa have also departed.

"West Ham United would like to thank Nuno, Rui and Rui for their hard work and commitment during their time at the Club, and wish them all the very best for the future.

"The process of recruiting a new Head Coach is already underway."

Mark Noble, Steve Potts and Gerard Prenderville will oversee the team for the trip to Cardiff.

While Nuno was fortunate to keep his job after relegation from the Premier League, it felt from the outside that he was doing a satisfactory job at the London Stadium.

Had West Ham beat Southampton and West Brom, they would be sitting top of the Championship, emphasising that the 52-year-old has essentially been sacked because of two defeats.

With a favourable fixture list coming up, there was every chance that Nuno would have kept West Ham in contention for the title.

Cardiff, Blackburn Rovers, Preston North End and Portsmouth are their next four games.

Nuno leaves his role with a record of 19 wins, 15 draws and 19 defeats from 53 matches across all competitions.

#1835. Bruno Fernandes sends Michael Carrick sack message after dramatic Manchester United victory

Bruno Fernandes has insisted that no-one’s job needed saving after Manchester United secured a dramatic 3-2 victory over Roma.

The Red Devils went into the Champions League clash off the back of a nine-match winless run that saw pressure pile on manager Michael Carrick, with most expecting him to be relieved of his duties following the 3-0 demolition by Bournemouth, which followed the 4-1 thrashing at Como.

He ultimately survived the sack and stayed on for another defeat, this time at Chelsea, and questions were being asked once more as United fell 2-0 down to the in-form Italian side inside 18 minutes at Old Trafford.

Matias Soule and Donyell Malen got the goals in an awful first half for the hosts, which was darkened by supporters throwing gold and green balloons and tennis balls from the stands onto the pitch in protest at the club’s plight, while colourful chanting was directed at the directors’ box, where Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada sat watching on.

Captain Fernandes, who was dropped by Carrick against Bournemouth for criticism he made about the manager’s approach in the Como defeat, missed a penalty and cut a frustrated figure at times on Tuesday, but luck smiled down on the Portuguese as he was able to reprieve himself from the spot after an encroachment allowed him to retake his 12-yard kick.

Afterwards, the No8 insisted that Carrick’s job was not in question in his first interview since his Como comments.

"No, we don't need to save anyone's job,” Fernandes said.

"The club needed that win, the players needed that win. It's something that we needed as a group of players together with the staff.

"We've been working so hard to get out of this situation altogether. It's been tough, there's been a lot of speculation in the media, a lot of lies around many things that have happened in this club. Between me and the manager, that we had cleared the air, then after, nothing of that happened.

"The manager took a decision of putting myself on the bench because I wasn't performing at that level. Everyone felt that it was a punishment for the words that I had. If it was, it was right.

"The manager is the one that makes the decisions. I have to accept them, I have to go forward with that. It doesn't change the belief I have in the manager, in the staff and every player that is in this club.

"It doesn't change my aim to win every game that I have ahead of me.

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Scott Parker is confident he can lead West Ham back to the Premier League after being appointed as the Hammers' new head coach on Wednesday.

Parker, who made 129 appearances for West Ham as a player, has put pen to paper on a two-and-a-half-year contract following the sacking of Nuno Espirito Santo.

West Ham made the decision to part ways with Nuno after back-to-back defeats to Southampton and West Brom, leaving them six points behind league leaders Middlesbrough.

Since replacing Graham Potter in September 2025, Nuno won just 19 of his 53 games in charge, while also failing to keep West Ham in the Premier League last season.

And they will be hoping to bounce back following the appointment of Parker, who has won promotion from the second tier three times with Fulham, Bournemouth and Burnley.

"It is a very proud moment for me to step into this role and return to a club that means so much to me and my family," Parker told West Ham's official website.

"A lot of very fond memories of my time here – four years of probably the best football I played in my career.

"More than anything, this is an opportunity that I am very excited about. I feel privileged and honoured to be the guy that wants to lead us back to the Premier League and be the head coach of this football club at this moment in time.

"My energy levels, my enthusiasm, my desire, my passion – it's absolutely running through and that's the feeling I had as soon as there was a conversation that this was possible.

"From my first calls with Karim [Virani] and Daniel [Kretinsky], it was clear they have a shared vision and desire to return the club to the Premier League as quickly as possible. I share that ambition, and I'm very confident we can achieve it.

#1832. Michael Carrick issues Manchester United injury latest after Carlos Baleba blow

Michael Carrick will be sweating over the fitness of Carlos Baleba after the Manchester United midfielder hobbled off on Tuesday.

The Cameroon international was forced off with a hamstring injury in the 3-2 victory over Roma at Old Trafford, as the Red Devils roared back from 2-0 down to secure a much-needed victory.

It is a result that eases the pressure on their under-fire manager, who had overseen a nine-match winless run which had seen his job brought into question.

Baleba was a bright spark for the home side in an otherwise absymal display, with the summer recruit showing bursts of energy from midfield, looking to support attacking moves.

An early power into the Roma box in the second period was what did the damage, however, as he pulled up grasping his hamstring in agony inside the first minute of the second half.

It comes as a fresh blow to the former Brighton midfielder, who arrived in the north west in the summer with a pre-existing ankle problem that scuppered his start to life in his new colours.

Carrick issued an update on Baleba afterwards, and he will be praying that his new signing will only be out for a short time.

#1831. Barcelona transfer news: truth behind PSG defender Willian Pacho rumour revealed

By Axel Clody | 03 Nov 2026 09:54

Reports have circulated in recent days about interest from Barcelona in Willian Pacho, and even a possible offer being prepared. The truth about this rumour has now come out.

Signed by Paris Saint-Germain in the summer of 2024 from Eintracht Frankfurt for €40m (£34m), Willian Pacho has stepped up to a new level. The Ecuadorian defender immediately established himself as an undisputed starter at left centre-back and is now regarded as one of the best in the world in his position.

The capital club are naturally satisfied with his performances and extended his contract until June 2031 at the start of the season. Both parties therefore appear ready to work together over the long term. However, the 25-year-old understandably attracts attention in the market.

At the start of September, Manchester City and Arsenal went to watch this key man of Luis Enrique’s side. Both English heavyweights are very interested in the Parisian’s profile and would like to add him to their defence. Real Madrid and Liverpool have also been described as suitors for Pacho.

More recently, Catalan outlet El Nacional also reported that Barcelona, who want to sign a centre-back this winter, were thinking about the Ecuador international for the next transfer window. The Catalan club would be prepared to part with Jules Kounde and Ronald Araujo to fund the move.

As this rumour started to circulate, Matteo Moretto gave an update on the situation. The Italian journalist insists, unsurprisingly, that Willian Pacho is not on the market. Luis Enrique greatly appreciates his defender and is counting on him for the rest of the season and for the future.

The player himself also wants to stay in Paris and keep winning trophies. So, for now, there are no discussions about a potential move to Barcelona. There is nothing in this story and, in any case, there is no chance of a Willian Pacho transfer to Barcelona taking place this winter.

Starting with the hosts, mounting what was an iconic Champions League comeback at Old Trafford on Tuesday night, both Michael Carrick and Manchester United claimed an essential European boost. Eventually dragging themselves to a remarkable 3-2 victory at home against Italian giants Roma, the Red Devils are now desperately searching for some crucial stability. However, despite drawing a line under their record-breaking nine-match winless rut, United are sensationally scrapping it out at the foot of the Premier League standings. Landing just a sole win from any of their first nine top-flight appearances and opening this weekend’s fixtures holding just a one-point buffer over slipping into the relegation zone, Carrick’s side also know the importance of finding some defensive grit. In fact, Manchester United are still waiting to put a maiden domestic clean sheet on the board since opening up the 2026/27 campaign.

While Brazilian international Matheus Cunha might have been shown a dramatic Champions League red card on Tuesday night, the ex-Wolves star is free to feature at Old Trafford. However, limping off in midweek with a reported hamstring injury, Manchester United will be without big-money summer recruit Carlos Baleba.

Carrick’s side have confirmed that former RB Leipzig striker Benjamin Sesko will miss the remainder of 2026 due to a long-term shin issue. Belgium international Youri Tielemans should be handed an immediate full recall in the middle of the park.

As for the visitors, completely blown away in Catalonia on Tuesday night as they slumped to a 3-0 drumming against Spanish icons Barcelona, Aston Villa will know the importance of immediately dusting themselves down. Watching their EFL Cup adventure come to a thumping end last week as they were hit with another 3-0 defeat against Bournemouth, Unai Emery’s men have failed to win their previous three appearances across all competitions. Despite finding a route into the top-half of the Premier League standings, Aston Villa will be concerned by their most recent trip to Old Trafford. Falling to a 3-1 loss when they last met Manchester United for a Premier League showdown back on March 15th, Villa are also seeking their own respective defensive grit. It should be noted, Emery’s side have mustered just a sole clean sheet from any of their previous six straight matchups outside of the Midlands.

Yet to make a maiden appearance this season after sustaining a long-term knee injury while away with Belgium at the 2026 World Cup, Aston Villa will once again be without Amadou Onana here. Likewise, one-time Manchester United defender Aaron Wan-Bissaka remains a doubt with a muscle injury.

Enjoying a sensational start to life at Villa Park and already notching five Premier League strikes, summer recruit and ex-Chelsea marksman Nicolas Jackson will lead the line in Manchester. Likewise, fellow summer arrival and Swiss starlet Johan Manzambi will join Jackson in the final third.

Producing a sensational Champions League comeback at Old Trafford on Tuesday night as they dragged themselves to a remarkable 3-2 victory, Manchester United will be desperate to use that gutsy performance as a platform to build on. However, still waiting to claim a maiden domestic clean sheet since opening up the 2026/27 campaign, Carrick’s side will meet an Aston Villa squad who are searching for their own essential boost on Sunday afternoon. Two camps who have shown their own defensive struggles so far this season, we could be set for an enjoyable Premier League battle this weekend.

Verdict: Nicolas Jackson over 0.5 shots on target

Prediction: Bayer Leverkusen vs Olympique Marseille

Liverpool will be reunited with a familiar face for this evening’s Champions League clash against Fenerbahce.

After Ismail Kartal resigned from his Fenerbahce post last week, Dirk Kuyt has been installed as the Turkish side’s interim boss which means he will face the club he played for between 2006 and 2012.

The Dutchman has got his work cut out to get Fenerbahce firing in this season’s league phase, having been thumped 6-0 by Aston Villa on matchday two and drawing with Roma and Slavia Prague.

Speaking in the pre-match press conference, Kuyt admitted he will need to keep his emotions in check for what he describes as an “special occasion”.

He said: "Of course, tomorrow will be a very special occasion for me but at the stage we're in, I'm not here for myself. I'm here for the club and that's what is important - to show the fans who deserve much more, a reaction, positive energy and a good performance."

Liverpool, meanwhile, have won all three games in the league phase so far, scoring 12 goals but have conceded seven as Andoni Iraola has not yet struck the right balance between attack and defence.

The Reds are seeking to bounce back from defeat to Arsenal at the weekend, though they can take confidence from the fact that they have won four of five away games across all competitions this season.

While Liverpool are no strangers to Turkey, particularly Istanbul, this will be the first-ever meeting with Fenerbahce at any level and the attacking talent across both squads suggests an entertaining game is on the cards.

#1827. Liverpool suffer new injury blow as official statement released before Fenerbahce

By Ben Knapton | 03 Nov 2026 09:57

Liverpool have announced that midfielder Ryan Gravenberch will miss Wednesday's Champions League clash with Fenerbahce due to a heel injury.

The Netherlands international was an unused substitute in Sunday's 1-0 Premier League defeat to Arsenal, when Trey Nyoni and Alexis Mac Allister were preferred in the middle of the park.

Andoni Iraola did not suggest that Gravenberch's omission was enforced, instead talking up the qualities of Nyoni, suggesting that his midfield selection was entirely tactical.

Gravenberch was therefore expected to be involved in Istanbul this week, but Liverpool released a statement on Tuesday morning confirming that the Dutchman would not be involved.

"Ryan Gravenberch has been ruled out of Liverpool’s Champions League fixture at Fenerbahce," the Reds said. "A heel injury means the midfielder will not be part of the Reds’ travelling squad for Wednesday’s meeting with the Turkish side in Istanbul. He will instead remain at the AXA Training Centre to undergo treatment with the club’s medical team."

At this stage, the severity of Gravenberch's injury remains unclear, although Iraola will likely be pressed for an update when he faces the media on Tuesday evening after landing in Turkey.

However, the 24-year-old can also be considered an early doubt for Sunday's Premier League clash with Crystal Palace, as his stop-start 2026-27 season at Anfield continues.

Gravenberch has played 12 times for Liverpool in all tournaments this term - providing one assist - but he has made just four Premier League starts due to a combination of factors.

The former Ajax man was sent off in the 3-0 home defeat to Manchester City and subsequently missed Liverpool's 2-1 win at Brentford through suspension, while Mac Allister, Nyoni and Dominik Szoboszlai have also provided fierce competition.

Gravenberch did complete the full 90 in each of Liverpool's last two Champions League games against LASK Linz and Villarreal, though, as well as the Reds' 2-0 Premier League success over Brighton & Hove Albion on October 25.

With Gravenberch sidelined, Nyoni and Mac Allister could join forces from the start once again, although Szoboszlai is another option after making a full recovery from a hamstring issue and subsequent setback.

Gravenberch is set to be one of five Liverpool absentees against Fenerbahce, a list that includes compatriot Jeremie Frimpong, whose thigh injury will keep him out until after the international break.

The Reds are also working without long-term Achilles victim Hugo Ekitike, whose return has been provisionally pencilled in for January, while Giovanni Leoni and Conor Bradley (knee) will not be back until the winter either.

Liverpool sit third in the Champions League league-phase table as one of just five teams to win all their games so far, alongside Real Betis, Real Madrid, Paris Saint-Germain and Aston Villa.

#1826. Hearts keeper Reus hopes to use inside knowledge of his old boss Reedijk to prolong Hibs manager's false start as they clash in derby

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER

Published: 18:43 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 18:49 EDT, 31 October 2026

When Hibs appointed Marink Reedijk just over a month ago, there weren’t many people within Scottish football who could claim to know much about the Dutchman.

Especially among the Hibs support, the response was one largely of bemusement as to why the club had taken a gamble on a 34-year-old rookie whose only previous experience was in the Belgian second tier.

At Beveren, Reedijk carved a reputation for himself as a coach who played high-octane attacking football as his side finished last season unbeaten as champions, duly winning promotion to the top flight.

It was an achievement and a style of play which was sufficiently impressive enough to alert the data boffins at Jamestown Analytics.

Back in the summer, Reedijk’s name had actually been on Hearts’ radar before they eventually chose to appoint Wouter Vrancken instead.

There was never any formal approach, but Hearts and Jamestown were aware of his name and his reputation as a young coach of considerable promise.

Whether or not Reedijk’s style of play could translate to the SPFL Premiership was a topic of much intrigue when he arrived to replace the sacked David Gray.

Reus denies Martin Boyle back in September's Edinburgh derby meeting

It is fair to say he has made something of an inauspicious start. In beginning his reign with defeats to Dundee United, Falkirk and Celtic, he became the first Hibs boss since Pat Fenlon to lose his opening three games.

He finally arrested that sequence courtesy of a 1-1 draw against St Mirren in midweek, but Hibs remain mired in relegation trouble.

Now comes the small matter of an Edinburgh derby against Hearts, with the rivals set to clash at Hampden this afternoon in the semi-finals of the Premier Sports Cup.

Reedijk desperately needs a victory to finally ignite his reign, with many Hibs fans already questioning whether this is a gamble that may backfire.

In the 2-1 defeat to Celtic last weekend, Hibs finished the match with Grant Hanley playing up front for the final ten minutes. It was an act of desperation and one which would see Reedijk take a lot of criticism.

Yet, although Reedijk is struggling to convince so far, there’s a man behind enemy lines who will happily sing his praises.

Reedijk picked up his first point as Hibs boss in the midweek draw at St Mirren

Hearts goalkeeper Beau Reus played under Reedijk for two years at Beveren. Reus insists he would be happy to go out on a limb and vouch that his old boss is a top-class operator.

As is always the way in football, friends can be found in unlikely places. Prior to a Hampden derby showdown, Reus opened up on his relationship with his fellow Dutchman during their time in Belgium.

‘We were together in Belgium the last two years,’ said the Hearts keeper, who has been excellent since making the switch to Tynecastle. ‘For me, he’s a good manager. His gameplan is really clear.

‘Hopefully that helps us a bit to crack the code. I will have a meeting with our coach to tell him how he will play, probably!

‘But Marink is very adaptable. He’s a young coach. I know he will have some tricks up his sleeve.

‘We are both Dutch and, as always, if you are a guy from an outside country that plays in Belgium, it’s normal you have a certain connection. He helped me grow a lot.

‘He’s really straight, so if he has a plan, he will go to implement his plan as well as he can. Off the pitch he’s a really, really nice guy, really warm. But, yeah, as soon as you’re on the pitch with him, you know exactly what you have to do for him. He makes very clear.

‘We are very kind to each other, but I think on Sunday we will forget about it for 90 minutes. After that, we can shake hands again.

‘I knew there were rumours that he was coming to Hibs, so the day I left for the last international break, I flew back to Amsterdam and his plane was just landing.

‘I said to my girlfriend it’s unbelievable that I come across him again in this way. But in football it is always like this, you will see each other many times.’

Reus is impressing for Hearts, with his shootout heroics securing a Conference League spot

Hearts come into the semi-final on the back of a 2-2 draw against Rangers at Tynecastle on Wednesday night, a match in which they were the better side for large spells.

Vrancken’s men are battling through an injury crisis which currently sees eight first-team regulars out of action.

‘It is devastating when you see so many injuries,’ noted Reus. ‘But we will play with the players we have and give 100 per cent for sure.’

It promises to be a thriller in Mount Florida as Reedijk’s Hibs go up against Vrancken’s Hearts. Two coaches renowned for front-foot attacking football, it’ll be anything but dull.

Reus insists it would be a major sign of the continued progress being made at Hearts if they can reach the final.

‘I don’t know the numbers off the top of my head, but the last time the club won this competition was quite some time ago,’ he said. ‘So it’s massive.

‘And of course, it’s always great to play for cups, playing in tournaments, because you don’t win that many trophies in your career, so every chance is one.

‘The fact it is a derby is great. We have already played Hibs before this season and beaten them at Easter Road.

‘You see how much tension and how much build-up there was to the game. Also in the stadium, how much they hated us! So, if you win, it’s extra nice.

‘It is another massive game and we really want to bounce back from the disappointment of losing the late goal against Rangers in midweek.’

#1825. AC Milan 3-1 Inter: Five things we learned – individual and tactical success

AC Milan clinched a massive victory in their home derby against Inter on Saturday, with several positives to take from the game as a result.

There wasn’t exactly an excess of optimism before the game among the Milan fans, following what was a poor mid-week defeat and a so-so start to the season. However, we didn’t see much of this in the big game, with two goals scored after just ten minutes.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It’s almost as if Gerry Cardinale manifested the win before the game and he certainly got to celebrate afterwards, even brought to tears in the mixed zone. He probably learnt a lot from this game and so did we, with several positives to highlight.

Without Diego Moreira, Adrien Rabiot and Mario Gila, Milan and Ruben Amorim struggled a lot in the mid-week clash against Bologna. Fortunately, the trio was back against Inter and the difference was clear as night and day.

All three played a big role, but the true difference-maker was Moreira, who was elctric from the start after bagging an early and lovely assist for Christian Pulisic. Six minutes later, in the 10th minute, he picked up a second from a corner kick, setting up Rabiot.

Inter got back into the game a little with their goal, making it 2-1, and it was a delicate moment in the game when Milan needed to stay focused. And yet again, it was Moreira who brought them out of trouble with a fantastic free-kick just before half-time.

San Siro erupted and the Belgian certainly showed that he has several tricks up his sleeve. On top of the attacking contribution, the Belgian was relentless throughout the game as he helped a tonne defensively until the final whistle.

Milan seem to have a game changer in their hands and it was fitting that he delivered this type of performance in his first Derby Della Madonnina. Especially since Ricky Kaka was in the stands, the player who made Moreira choose the No.22 shirt.

Milan did an outstanding job up front, being as clinical as they could be, but Inter were always going to create chances on the other end. So, it was even more impressive how the Rossoneri managed to contain them, especially in the second half.

There were some struggling moments in the first half, but in that period, Mike Maignan came up big with multiple good saves. One of them was just phenomenal, as he had little to no time to react and it was all about the Frenchman’s reflexes, which didn’t let him down.

That was a crucial moment in the game, with the result being 2-1 for Milan and with an equaliser there, the game could’ve been a lot different.

In the second half, the Rossoneri were a lot more compact and it was more about the players in front of Maignan. Strahinja Pavlovic stepped up a tonne after the half-time mark as he was a tad shaky in the opening 45 minutes, especially against Spence who was bursting down that flank.

Gila was also very solid on the right-hand side and especially when he was on the ball. It’s a completely different team when he’s on the pitch.

Diawara, Musah and Modric also did a very fine job closing down the spaces and handling Inter’s press well, with the Croatian rolling the years back as he was relentless throughout the game.

It was a very impressive defensive performance and especially in the second half of the game, as it seems Amorim’s instructions at the break limited Inter even further.

I purposefully left out Koni De Winter from the previous point because I think the Belgian deserves a section all for himself.

In the absence of Lautaro, Thuram was always going to be the main threat. Not just because he has five goals and four assists in the opening eight games, but also because he has done very well in the derby before.

So naturally, if Milan were to win the game, they had to neutralise the Frenchman and it was clear from the beginning that De Winter’s instructions were to stay close to the striker and not give him breathing space.

De Winter deserves all the praise here because he won almost all of the duels against the striker, effectively frustrating him and getting him out of the game completely. The only memory I have from Thuram was when he dropped almost into his own half towards the end of the game to try and make something happen, but that was not nearly enough.

Aside from his battle with the Frenchman, De Winter also did well with his passing and overall game and was arguably the best Milan defender on the night.

Really positive performance and he needs to keep it up, because conceding silly goals has been a problem for Milan and they clearly have the quality to prevent them.

We already mentioned the brilliant work at the back and the saves Maignan made, but it’s only fair to praise the attack too as they also did a fine job. Milan had three shots on goal until the 90th minute and had scored three goals, which is impressive considering how wasteful the Rossoneri have been in attack in the last few games.

The team started off with the right mindset and put pressure on Inter early on, with some great individual runs such as the one from Moreira. All of the chances were finished with clinical precision, which is exactly what you need to win in the big games.

We already praised Moreira, but Pulisic was also very good as he found the empty space on the opener and buried it to give his side the lead. He then continued playing well between the lines and he was smart about controlling the game after his side was ahead.

Rabiot came in clutch again with yet another goal and a positive performance overall, even if he had to do a bit more running in the second half and focus on the defensive aspect of the game.

I know he failed to score or assist again, but that doesn’t mean Goncalo Ramos was necessarily bad. He pressed quite a bit and he opened up spaces for his teammates. You can clearly see on Milan’s second goal how he pushes Sucic towards the byline so he can’t charge towards Rabiot after Moreira’s corner.

Again, he absolutely needs to be more involved in the box but he’s still a very valuable player on the pitch.

There was obviously a bittersweet feeling coming into the derby after losing to Bologna in such a frustrating manner, but the availability of Moreira, Rabiot and Gila gave Amorim and the fans some enthusiasm prior to the game.

To Amorim’s credit, he picked the correct starting eleven and his team had the right mindset from the start. The coach was aware of Inter’s fragile defending and instructed his team to raise the intensity from the start and apply pressure, which worked a treat with two goals in the opening ten minutes.

Inter then tried to come back into the game and created a few chances, it’s fair to say, but Amorim again tweaked something at the half-time break. His team was more compact and more aggressive after that, which almost completely neutralised Inter.

The coach also waited with his subs, which I think was correct given the team was playing well and there weren’t obvious signs of fatigue. When the changes did come, I think they were spot on.

More importantly, the whole game management was impressive. The game started off with Milan playing in Amorim’s style, which resulted in the goals but also exposed his team and then in the second half, Milan were more compact and not eager to press or attack as much.

On top of that, there were numerous times when the Rossoneri kept the ball, were patient and avoided risk and I think the tempo was dictated by Milan despite Inter having a bit more possession towards the end. Excellent from the coach.

#1824. How to watch Slavia Prague vs Arsenal: TV channel and live stream for Champions League today

The Standard's journalism is supported by our readers. If you click links to other sites on this page, we will earn commission.

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal face Slavia Prague in the Champions League tonight, exactly a year on from their last visit to the Czech Republic.

Prague, meanwhile, have picked up just one point from their opening three Champions League fixtures, losing to Lens and competition debutants Sabah, but did claw back a two-goal deficit against Fenerbahce to earn a point.

Ahead of Wednesday's game at Cardiff City, West Ham sit in eighth position in the Championship table.

Parker has been out of work since April when leaving his role with Burnley after nearly two seasons in charge.

However, the former West Ham midfielder is an obvious appointment, partly due to winning three player of the year awards during his previous time at the club.

His understanding of the club's culture is another reason why he has allegedly been handed the reins at the London Stadium.

#1821. Manchester United: Michael Carrick reveals half-time team talk that may have saved his job

Michael Carrick has detailed the half-time team talk which inspired Manchester United’s come-from-behind win over Roma, and could save his job.

An extraordinary Champions League night at Old Trafford had started grimly, featuring renewed fan demonstrations directed at owners the Glazer family alongside a feeble first-half performance that the visitors ruthlessly punished.

Matias Soule seized on an avoidable opener before Donyell Malen doubled the lead from the spot, prompting loud boos at the interval, before Carrick’s side dug deep to pull off a memorable turnaround.

Captain Bruno Fernandes converted a retaken penalty prior to Matheus Cunha scoring a dramatic late double – and receiving an even later red card – as the Red Devils halted their nine-game winless run in style.

"[’I’m] proud of a lot of people, actually," United head coach Carrick said. "Proud of the players. I think they deserve a lot of credit for pulling through that in a tough situation.

"And for the supporters, you know, to be there. I could feel they were desperate for us to give them something to get their teeth into.

"Frustrating, disappointing, as we all were going in at half-time.

“But I spoke with the players about the second half, about what this place can do and moments, and one moment can really flip it.

"We came out second half really well, just stayed really positive through the whole second half.

"To come through and see so many positives and had to keep going to get that at the end, I’m really pleased for an awful lot of people for that one.

"It’s one win, so we’re not getting too carried away with things, but it was it was an important one for us."

He added: “It’s important for some of the players to have the feeling that they maybe haven’t had here before.

“Some of the lads that came this year, some of the boys that came even last year who maybe haven’t had a feeling of that.

#1819. Manchester United in agreement over Michael Carrick sack decision after Roma win

Michael Carrick has eased pressure on his job with Manchester United ‘s come-from-behind win over Roma, but the threat of the sack remains alive.

The under-pressure manager ended a run of three straight defeats - and nine games without a win - as Matheus Cunha scored twice, and was sent off, late on to down an under-strength Roma side.

Roma had raced into a 2-0 lead inside 17 minutes thanks an early Matias Soule strike and a Donyell Malen penalty. But Bruno Fernandes halved the deficit shortly after half-time before Cunha’s late double.

Carrick will now hope his team have momentum ahead of a crucial clash with Aston Villa on Sunday before the international break. The head coach will now that he is not yet out of the woods.

United's hierarchy held crisis talks over the head coach's position after a 3-0 defeat home defeat to the hands Bournemouth earlier in October.

Chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox were involved in discussions at Carrington the following days, with replacements reportedly considered.

Aston Villa boss Unai Emery, former Newcastle manager Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann, fresh from leaving Germany, are among the names who continue to be linked with the vacancy. Antonio Conte has also been mentioned as a possible option.

However, United opted against making an immediate change last month, allowing Carrick to remain in charge for defeat at Chelsea and Tuesday’s late triumph over Roma.

According to The Athletic, Man Utd chiefs last week agreed to keep Carrick in post for the visit of Roma and Sunday’s visit of Aston Villa in the Premier League before reassessing the situation during the break.

That stance is not expected to change despite a much-needed victory.

Man Utd chiefs are said to be happy for Carrick to remain in charge until the international break being next week, at which point a new manager could be appointed and given extra time to settle in the job before domestic football returns later in November.

#1818. Arsenal transfer news: Martin Zubimendi ready to leave this winter, seven European giants informed

By Axel Clody | 03 Nov 2026 10:31, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 10:31

Short of game time at Arsenal, Martin Zubimendi is ready to leave the London club in the January transfer window. Seven European clubs have been informed.

In the summer of 2025, Arsenal beat several clubs, notably Real Madrid, to sign Martin Zubimendi. Arsenal spent £59.5m (€70m) to sign the Spain midfielder from Real Sociedad. After an encouraging first season, the 27-year-old is having a difficult start to the campaign.

He has made 10 appearances and has started only twice, both in the EFL Cup. Martin Zubimendi has played just 15 minutes in the Champions League and 99 in the Premier League. He has become a rotation player in Mikel Arteta’s mind. This situation is hard for the Spain international to accept.

According to TeamTalk, Zubimendi is ready to leave Arsenal in January to try to relaunch his career. He wants more playing time. Many major European clubs are aware of this decision taken by the midfielder.

Real Madrid, Barcelona and Atletico Madrid have all shown an interest in a return to La Liga for the former Real Sociedad man. Real Madrid have been long-term admirers of the San Sebastian native.

It remains to be seen whether this opportunity will change the plans of Real Madrid, who had decided not to sign anyone this winter.

In Germany, Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund have been informed of the possibility of signing Martin Zubimendi this winter. The same goes for Chelsea and Liverpool in England. It remains to be seen whether one of these European giants will now be ready to make a move this winter.

In this affair, Arsenal are aware of their player’s desire to leave the club this winter and are preparing to open the door for him.

A loan departure is a possible option. It would notably allow Arsenal, who invested £59.5m (€70m) a little over a year ago, to hope that Zubimendi relaunches himself in the second half of the season so as to secure a higher transfer fee next summer.

#1817. GdS: An ‘achievable dream’ – why Cardinale left Italy ‘convinced’ by Scudetto bid

Gerry Cardinale left San Siro after the derby win over Inter with a distinct feeling: this AC Milan team can challenge for the title.

Happy as ever about the derby victory, yet still rueful over the defeat to Bologna – a stumble that must not be repeated – La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) write that Cardinale departed Italy yesterday, bound for New York, where his family and work await him.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

His thoughts however remain firmly fixed on AC Milan and the tasks that lie ahead, with the renewal of Adrien Rabiot’s contract as a short-term priority and the Scudetto as a cherished, long-term dream.

He admitted as much following the loss to Raffaele Palladino’s side, and he feels it even more strongly now, having won his first derby since taking direct personal control of the club on May 25th.

On Sunday evening, following the final whistle, Cardinale chose not to speak to the team. He had already said everything he needed to say to his players on Saturday at Milanello, aiming to motivate and spur them on to bounce back from the 4-2 defeat against Bologna.

The team took his words to heart: after the derby, Maignan and his team-mates could see the joy on Cardinale’s face, even though he didn’t utter a single word. Amorim, who granted the squad two days of (training set to resume tomorrow) offered his own praise for the team’s performance.

The head of RedBird Capital stepped away from the dressing room, wanting the moment to remain special for the players and the coaching staff, but also because he was deeply moved—tears nearly welling up in his eyes.

Milan, its fans, and the project itself all needed a night like this, and the American knew it. Now, however, Gerry expects the level of performance shown in the derby to be replicated in the upcoming matches, specifically the two before the break: Thursday against Ferencváros and Sunday in Genoa.

These are fixtures that will require managing the post-derby euphoria to ensure there is no drop in focus. While some of the squad celebrated at a well-known Milanese nightclub on Saturday night, the focus shifts to Europe starting tomorrow.

The position in the table needs to be improved following the slip-ups against Benfica and Bournemouth in the first three games. Beyond that, further progress will be required in Serie A.

The only way to close the seven-point gap on Lazio is to avoid any further stumbles like the one against Bologna. On this point, Cardinale and Amorim are in complete agreement.

In fact, while both were delighted by the triumph over their city rivals, that joy only sharpened their regret over the three points dropped against the Rossoblù. Neither the manager nor the owner could stomach the collapse from a 2-1 lead at halftime to a 4-2 defeat.

The two spoke after the derby and are fully aligned: injuries notwithstanding, a Milan side that aspires to be Milan once again – both in Italy and in Europe – cannot afford such lapses in focus.

Beating Inter is satisfying, and remaining unbeaten against their rivals for eight consecutive matches is a positive, but the ultimate priority remains lifting a trophy. City supremacy is not enough, not for Cardinale, and not for Amorim.

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal face Slavia Prague in the Champions League tonight, with William Saliba closing in on a return and Max Dowman pushing to start.

Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes appeared to be on the verge of tears as he embraced the travelling faithful following his side's latest defeat.

Fernandes returned to the United side after being dropped for their loss against Bournemouth last week, when he was an unused substitute.

The decision from Michael Carrick came after his skipper had criticised Carrick's tactics in the 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como, leading to uncertainty around the duo's relationship.

In the week, however, they held crisis talks to fix their relationship, and Fernandes was back in the team – and playing 90 minutes – against Chelsea on Saturday.

Yet he was unable to turn around his side's fortunes, with United falling to a 2-0 defeat, and the club have now gone nine games in all competitions without a win.

And he appeared to be in a battle to hold back the tears as United's players headed over to the away end at full-time, showing how much the team's poor form is affecting him.

A visibly emotional Bruno Fernandes after another disappointing result for Man Utd 💔 pic.twitter.com/E4MhUoD8VW

Bruno Fernandes appeared to be fighting back the tears following Manchester United's defeat by Chelsea

Carrick has made a habit of applauding the fans first after the game, and was cheered off following the Bournemouth defeat before those in attendance turned on the players.

On this occasion, Carrick again walked down the tunnel without his players, but the team were in fact cheered.

Fernandes was stood alone, and repeatedly wiped his face as he took in the situation.

'He's a big player, Bruno,' Carrick said after the game. 'He offers us so much, you know, with his experience.

'He's been through a lot here and achieved a lot and shown what he can bring to the team.

'So he's an important part of the team for us and I think we've got a good balance today. We've got a good team and the boys are looking forward to it.'

#1812. Prediction: Bayer Leverkusen vs Olympique Marseille

Bayer Leverkusen will look to maintain their flawless start to the Europa League when they welcome Marseille to the BayArena on Thursday evening.

The German side have won all three of their league-phase fixtures and sit second in the standings, while Marseille find themselves in a desperate position after losing each of their opening three matches and slipping towards an early European exit.

Leverkusen have been one of the standout performers in this season’s Europa League.

Carles Martinez’s men have taken maximum points from their first three outings, scoring eight goals without conceding once. Their latest continental success came in a controlled 2-0 victory over OFI Crete, further strengthening their position among the competition’s frontrunners.

Domestic form has been less convincing. Since that win in Greece, Leverkusen have suffered two Bundesliga defeats and were most recently beaten 4-2 by Stuttgart, a result that dropped them to sixth in the table and ended their perfect home record for the season.

Even so, BayArena remains a difficult venue. Leverkusen won their first five home matches of the campaign, and their European performances there have been particularly authoritative.

The biggest concern for Martinez is an injury crisis in attack. Eliesse Ben Seghir, Martin Terrier, Christian Kofane and Moussa Diaby are all unavailable, significantly reducing options in the final third.

Patrik Schick is expected to lead the line again, supported by Lucas Vazquez, Ibrahim Maza and Afonso Moreira.

With right-back Guela Doue unavailable too, former Liverpool defender Jarell Quansah is likely to get the nod.

Marseille’s Europa League campaign is rapidly becoming a crisis.

The French club have lost all three of their league-phase fixtures and are currently languishing near the bottom of the standings. Their hopes of qualification are fading quickly, meaning another defeat could leave them facing an uphill battle to remain in the competition.

Ironically, domestic form has improved considerably. Bruno Genesio’s side have won four consecutive Ligue 1 matches and climbed closer to the European qualification places in France.

However, concerns remain, particularly away from home. Marseille have lost seven of their last 10 away matches in all competitions and have already suffered four defeats in six road fixtures this season.

Defensively, inconsistency continues to be a problem. While Marseille have scored freely during their recent resurgence, they have also struggled to keep clean sheets, conceding seven goals across their last six games.

Amine Gouiri is expected to spearhead the attack, with support coming from a midfield trio likely to feature Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg, Himad Abdelli and Tochukwu Nnadi.

Left-back Emerson Palmieri might be given a rest after he avoided serious injury against Toulouse on Sunday, in which case his place should be taken by Ulisses Garcia.

Marseille’s recent domestic improvement suggests they should provide a sterner challenge than their Europa League results indicate.

However, their struggles away from home and poor defensive record in Europe make this a difficult assignment. Leverkusen have already demonstrated their ability to control matches at this level and continue to look far more balanced despite their attacking injury problems.

The visitors may create opportunities, but Leverkusen’s European confidence and home advantage should be enough to extend their perfect start to the league phase.

#1811. Manchester United co-owners INEOS sack manager as official statement released

INEOS have sacked Lausanne-Sport manager Luka Elsner after just five months in charge, amid ongoing pressure on Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick.

The Swiss club, which is part-owned by Sir Jim Ratcliffe's INEOS group, confirmed on Tuesday that they had mutually agreed to end their relationship with the 44-year-old.

Elsner was appointed on 1 June but struggled to make an impact, winning eight of his 12 Swiss Super League matches. Lausanne's poor start to the campaign left them bottom of the table, prompting the club to make a change.

A statement read: “After lengthy discussions about the current sporting situation, FC Lausanne-Sport and Luka Elsner have mutually agreed to end their collaboration.”

His departure comes at a difficult time for INEOS at Manchester United, where Carrick is facing scrutiny following a disappointing run of results.

United's supporters have made their frustration with the club's ownership clear in recent weeks, directing criticism towards Ratcliffe and the Glazer family.

Protests continued during Tuesday's Champions League meeting with Roma, when fans threw green and gold balloons on to the pitch in the 21st minute while chanting against the owners.

The atmosphere improved after United produced a second-half comeback to secure a 3-2 victory. Bruno Fernandes scored from the penalty spot before Matheus Cunha struck twice to complete the turnaround.

However, the result is unlikely to remove the pressure on Carrick, who remains under scrutiny as United attempt to improve their domestic form.

The decision to part company with Elsner after such a short period is also likely to attract attention given INEOS' involvement in both clubs.

Celta Vigo defender Javi Rodriguez is attracting interest from a number of clubs across Europe, writes Sam Tabuteau.

Despite reports, though, there has not yet been any contact from Fulham for the 23-year-old.

Rodriguez made his Spain debut in June and is expected to attract interest in January.

Real Madrid are confident of winning the race to sign Manchester United teenager JJ Gabriel, who has not returned to Old Trafford since leaving the club in September.

Carrick will now hope his team have momentum ahead of a crucial clash with Aston Villa on Sunday before the international break. The head coach will now that he is not yet out of the woods.

Sunderland have announced that Brian Brobbey has signed a new long-term contract.

Pascal De Maesschalck has admitted he was surprised to be appointed Arsenal's academy director.

The Belgian began work at Arsenal in the summer, arriving from Strasbourg where he had been technical director since 2024.

De Maesschalck oversees the Gunners' academy programme, taking over from Per Mertesacker after he left at the end of last season having been in the role for eight years.

In an interview with Sporza, De Maesschalck revealed he viewed the interview process with Arsenal as a good opportunity in itself, before he ended up then getting the job.

Scott Parker is set to succeed Nuno Espirito Santo as West Ham head coach.

Nuno was relieved of his duties with immediate effect on Tuesday morning following back-to-back home defeats to Southampton and West Brom.

The Irons are four points off the automatic promotion places and have won six of their opening 13 Championship games this season.

West Ham invested heavily over the summer, breaking the Championship transfer record to sign midfielder Arne Engels from Celtic for £22million, and were among the favourites for promotion back to the Premier League.

Now, though, after a mixed start to the season, they have decided to part ways with Nuno and have landed on club legend Parker to take the reins as they look to get their promotion bid back on track.

Well, West Ham are not wasting any time in finding a replacement for Nuno Espirito Santo.

The Hammers announced this morning that they had parted company with Nuno and now the Athletic claim an agreement has been struck with former midfielder with Scott Parker.

There is hope Parker will be in appointed in time to take charge for Wednesday’s match against Cardiff.

Chelsea and Liverpool have both made approaches to sign Brentford left-back El Hadji Malick Diouf ahead of next summer’s transfer window.

The 21-year-old Senegal international only joined the Bees towards the end of the summer window but has already attracted interest from two Premier League rivals.

According to D Sports, both clubs have contacted Diouf’s agent to register their interest. The defender is under contract until 2031.

No decision has been made over his future, but a potential departure could develop sooner than expected.

West Ham have sacked Nuno Espirito Santo as head coach.

A statement reads: “West Ham United can confirm that men’s first-team Head Coach Nuno Espirito Santo has left his position with immediate effect.

“Following a thorough review of the start to the EFL Championship season, the Board of Directors believe that a change is necessary at this time in order to ensure that the Club’s objectives and expectations remain on track.

“Assistant Head Coach Rui Pedro Silva and Goalkeeper Coach Rui Barbosa have also departed.

“West Ham United would like to thank Nuno, Rui and Rui for their hard work and commitment during their time at the Club, and wish them all the very best for the future.

“The process of recruiting a new Head Coach is already underway.”

#1808. Man United, Bayern Munich 'in mix' for teenage star as Erik ten Hag confirms "concrete offers"

By Matt Law | 03 Nov 2026 11:46, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 11:48

Manchester United and Bayern Munich are reportedly both interested in signing FC Twente’s Ruud Nijstad during next summer's transfer window.

Nijstad, 18, is believed to be on the radar of a number of major clubs, with Twente facing a battle to keep hold of him on a long-term basis given his development.

According to Twente Insite, both Man United and Bayern are keen to secure his signature next year, while a number of other European teams are in the race.

Twente are in a strong position when it comes to the defender's future given that he signed a new contract in July until the summer of 2029.

Nijstad featured on 24 occasions for Twente last season and has played 17 times in all competitions during the 2026-27 campaign.

In total, the centre-back has played 41 times for his current team, scoring twice and registering one assist, while he has been capped twice by Netherlands Under-19s.

Former Man United manager Erik ten Hag has been Twente's technical director since February, and the Dutchman recently commented on the teenager's future.

“I don’t know, but there is indeed interest in him. Several clubs from the top eight in Europe have made concrete offers. But he simply made a very conscious choice to play for FC Twente this season,” said Ten Hag.

“He is a very great talent who joined the team last season. He is still very young, but he does so in a very self-assured manner. It is a pleasure to work with that boy. Quite a few clubs from the top of Europe have come forward. I think that is only a good thing.

“It is also particularly nice that he very consciously chose to stay with Twente for at least another year. Maybe even longer, but in any case, this season.”

It is well-known that Man United are preparing to overhaul their defence next summer.

It is possible that four new defenders could make the move to Old Trafford in the summer of 2027, including a right-back and a left-back.

Lisandro Martinez and Harry Maguire could both leave next summer, meanwhile, with two new centre-backs therefore potentially being targeted.

Leny Yoro is regarded as a key part of the Man United defence moving forwards, but there is also uncertainty surrounding the futures of both Ayden Heaven and Matthijs de Ligt.

#1806. Man United transfer news: Red Devils 'alerted' to potential summer availability of Bayern Munich attacker who could replace Bruno Fernandes

By Matt Law | 03 Nov 2026 12:08, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 12:10

Manchester United have reportedly been 'alerted' to the possibility that Lennart Karl could leave Bayern Munich during next summer's transfer window.

The 18-year-old has represented Bayern's first team on 52 occasions, scoring 10 goals and registering 10 assists in the process.

The four-time Germany international has a contract at Allianz Arena until the summer of 2029, but there is currently a host of speculation surrounding his future.

Recent comments from Bayern's honorary president Uli Hoeness on Karl are not believed to have been well-received by the youngster's reprensentatives.

"He is far from being a superstar," Hoeness told Welt am Sonntag. "Young players need humility. I don’t know whether it is good for Lennart Karl to always be over-protected. The comparisons with [Michael] Olise do not help him at all. There is still a massive difference between them."

According to Bild, the comments have caused 'unrest' in the Karl camp, which has alerted Man United to a possible transfer next summer.

The report claims that Liverpool and Arsenal are also keeping a close eye on the situation, with the teenager potentially available for £50m next summer.

Real Madrid have also been credited with an interest in Karl in recent weeks.

Earlier this year, Karl called Real Madrid his "dream club".

“Bayern is a very very big club. It's a dream to play there. But at some point I definitely want to go to Real Madrid. That's my dream club. Of course, Bayern is something very special and it's a lot of fun at the club," Karl told Sky Deutschland.

Karl's comments did not go down well with Bayern, and it is believed that there is friction behind the scenes, which could ultimately lead to a departure.

The teenager has scored once and registered two assists in 12 appearances for Bayern at the start of the 2026-27 campaign.

Karl largely operates as a number 10, but he can also feature off the right, and the German could potentially be a long-term replacement for Bruno Fernandes at Old Trafford.

Fernandes has struggled this season, and the 32-year-old's contract is due to expire at the end of the campaign, albeit with the option to extend for a further year.

#1805. Tottenham must be ‘nastier’ to be a perfect team, says De Zerbi

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Roberto De Zerbi says Tottenham are a different team to the one before the international break, but he believes they must become "nastier" to continue their upward trajectory.

Spurs beat 10-man Crystal Palace 2-0 last time out, winning three consecutive Premier League matches for the first time since February 2025.

It has been a complete turnaround from the results they produced before the extended international break in September, with the club at one point sitting at the bottom of the table.

Archie Gray and Jan Paul van Hecke were on target against Palace, who saw Jean-Philippe Mateta sent off for a nasty challenge on Micky van de Ven in the 13th minute.

Spurs make the trip to Elland Road on Saturday to face Leeds United, and De Zerbi said just a few areas of his team need fine-tuning before they are at the peak of their powers.

"I'm happy with the performance because we showed to be mature with clear ideas, and we didn't concede a counter-attack, maybe just one in the second half," he said.

"We created many, many chances. If we want to be perfect, we have to be nastier. But it's an individual thing, because if I'm the number nine or the number 10, I want to score.

"But I can't say anything. We are improving our physical condition. If we compare Tottenham before the national break and after the national break, now we are playing as a team.

"Before the international break, we had a lot of good players, but we weren't playing as a team."

Through the lens at Hotspur Way. @Betano_UK https://t.co/i36IylMMJ5

— Tottenham Hotspur (@SpursOfficial) November 4, 2026

Leeds, meanwhile, were on the end of a 2-0 defeat to Bournemouth, who have now won their last six matches across all competitions without conceding a goal.

But Leeds only had themselves to blame for going behind, with James Trafford at fault for Bournemouth's opener.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Harry Wilson spurned glorious chances before Trafford's loose pass was picked off by Justin Kluivert, who squared for Evanilson to score.

Amine Adli scored Bournemouth's second in second-half stoppage time, but Daniel Farke did not blame his goalkeeper for his blunder at the Vitality Stadium.

"It was self-inflicted, an own goal. This was decisive. Overall, we played a good away game," Farke said of the incident. "We don't have to speak about it.

"He is a terrific young goalkeeper and has saved us points this season. It's the life of a football player. The sun isn't always shining.

"But he will save us way more points than perhaps he cost us. We win together; we lose together. My recommendation is that he doesn't watch the game back. Football can have annoying days; it's an annoying day for him."

Despite seeing a goal ruled out against Bournemouth last time out, Calvert-Lewin continues to be Leeds' most attacking threat, though his work off the ball often goes unnoticed.

Calvert-Lewin has applied more high-intensity pressures in the opponent's penalty area than any other Premier League player this season (118), while he's also made the third-highest number of off-the-ball runs ending in the box (75).

Since the start of last season, only Bruno Fernandes (22), Rayan Cherki (14), Jarrod Bowen (11) and Declan Rice (10) have more Premier League assists than Kudus (eight).

In addition, of the nine players to have completed the most dribbles in the Premier League this season (17+), four of them play for Spurs, with Kudus joint-second on 21.

Despite being slightly favoured by the Opta supercomputer, Leeds have picked up just five points in their last 13 Premier League matches against Spurs (W1 D2 L10) and have not kept a clean sheet in any of their last 16 against them.

But they will be hoping to improve in the final third. Spurs have had the fourth-most shots in the Premier League this season (148), but rank in the bottom half for expected goals (11.7). Indeed, they have the lowest xG per shot of any side this term (0.08).

#1804. 'Why I'm here': Scott Parker sends message to West Ham fans in first words as new manager

West Ham have confirmed the appointment of Scott Parker as their new manager.

The former Hammers midfielder has quickly been appointed on a two-and-a-half year contract to succeed Nuno Espirito Santo, who was sacked on Monday following a disappointing start to the Championship season.

Parker had been out of work since leaving Burnley by mutual consent in April following confirmation of their relegation from the Premier League and is a second-tier promotion specialist, having previously led Bournemouth, Fulham and Burnley to the top-flight.

His two-decade playing career included a memorable four-year stint at West Ham between 2007-11, where he made 129 appearances across all competitions and won back-to-back Player of the Season awards after joining from Newcastle in a £7million move.

Parker - who also played for Chelsea and Charlton - eventually left for rivals Tottenham in 2011 after handing in a transfer request, staying at Spurs for two seasons before finishing his career at Fulham.

“It is a very proud moment for me to step into this role and return to a Club that means so much to me and my family,” Parker said. “A lot of very fond memories of my time here - four years of probably the best football I played in my career.

“There was a warmth, a love, a feeling that I probably didn’t have anywhere else. There was something which stood out constantly and that was the relationship that I built up with the fanbase here. That rapport and respect, that I felt instantly.

#1803. Pioli discusses current Milan team, relationship with Ibrahimovic, Scudetto win and Moreira

Stefano Pioli shared some more insight on his time as AC Milan head coach, including the impact of Zlatan Ibrahimovic, Rafael Leao and others.

Pioli was a guest on Sky Calcio Club after Juventus 2-0 Napoli last night, and he revisited the 2021-22 Scudetto win, discussing some of the characteristics of the players, and also drawing comparisons with some current squad members. MilanVibes relayed his words.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Firstly, the coach was asked about if he saw a bit of Rafael Leao in Diego Moreira, given the Belgian was the hero of the derby on Saturday night with one goal and two assists.

“I saw him against Sassuolo too, and he impressed me. He and Rabiot are really strong. Milan played a great match, Maignan made a great save… but with their starting eleven, they’re a really strong team. When Amorim made a few more substitutions, they struggled more.

“It took them a while to get to this point because they had players arriving, probably with some problems, and it takes time to find their rhythm and fitness.

“The results are showing. Modric also still has some important strength. Gonçalo Ramos is doing a great job for the team and is a very good player.”

The discussion about Milan inevitably brought them back to the team that won the league title in 2022. Pioli explained how the playing system was built around the characteristics of the players available, with particular attention to the defensive line and the ability to sustain aggressive football.

“A coach’s skill lies in adapting to a player’s characteristics. At AC Milan, I had players who got lost defending deep. I like that style of play, but it was the best one for those players.

“Kalulu and Tomori also allowed us to take risks. If you want to stay high up the pitch, you need to have significant intensity; anything in between doesn’t work.”

Pioli commented on Leao again, who reached the peak of his powers under the Italian, but also admitted that after the Scudetto not everything went as he would have hoped.

The Scudetto year was devastating. I’ve seen few players of that level. Then he wasn’t, and we weren’t, good. Because when you win, it’s because something special is created in the team. Paolo [Maldini], Ricky [Massara], and I weren’t good – and neither was he – at maintaining and further raising his level.

“He certainly has important qualities. The coach has to understand the players. Rafa is a good player who needs to be encouraged in a certain way.”

During the segment, the background on Roma’s interest also emerged. The Giallorossi contacted Pioli, but at that point the coach had already received an offer from Al Nassr.

“There were times when everyone called me. Even Roma, but I had just received my contract with Al Nassr and I couldn’t break my word.

“I don’t regret going to Saudi Arabia. I wanted to gain experience abroad after my years with AC Milan. The financial aspect and the opportunity to coach Cristiano Ronaldo also played a role.

“If you don’t coach him, you don’t understand how great he is. He’s a champion, obsessed with preparing to score goals. He’s very respectful.”

Pioli spoke about Zlatan Ibrahimovic and Cristiano Ronaldo, two of the biggest profiles that he has had to manage in his career to date.

“Cristiano and Zlatan have a very similar relationship: ‘You’re clear with me and I respect you, if you’re not clear with me, it’s no good.’ I’ve always based our relationship on clarity and sincerity.

“It’s clear that with Zlatan and Cristiano, if you tell them, ‘Look, you’re not playing tomorrow, or you’ll play 60 minutes tomorrow,’ and then I’ll take you off, and you do it or you don’t, it makes a difference.

“I didn’t tell Zlatan something once, but I didn’t tell him because in the rush, I think during the Covid period, we were playing every three days. At the end of the first half it was 0-0, then in 10 minutes we scored 2-3 goals, I don’t remember now…

“Anyway, I made three substitutions: I remember Zlatan, Calhanoglu, and another. So quick, but I hadn’t told Zlatan in advance… The next day [laughs]. he came to me… The good thing about Zlatan is that as soon as he gets over it, the next day it’s as if nothing had happened.”

When asked if Ibrahimovic frequently sulked, Pioli replied: “No, absolutely not. He’s great. But does he tell you? Yes, yes, and then with a tone…

“I always leave my office door open because I like to greet the players and see them. In fact, I had the office changed because I wanted it to be between the locker room and physiotherapy, which they have to go to every day anyway, so every day I greeted all the players, and they came in to see me.

“Every now and then I stopped them, but I didn’t stop them. That day, I didn’t expect Zlatan to come in. He came in and said, ‘I’ll speak today.’ You know, those chairs that move around, I danced for 2-3 minutes, but then it went away.”

Pioli also recalled his first meeting with the Swede, who arrived at Milanello at the end of January 2020 and undoubtedly played a key role in the resurgence.

“Ibrahimovic arrived at Milanello the first day. I waited for him there, and he arrived when it was dark. It was January, the end of January. I followed him in his training, but he also had a knee problem.

“He did a bit of treadmill work, then he came to my office, spoke to me a bit, and I explained to him how I wanted to use him on the pitch, technically and tactically. He said to me: ‘You’re the coach, I’m the player. You respect me, I’ll respect you.’ And that’s what happened.”

Pioli also spoke about the relationship between results and the team, explaining why it’s often more difficult for a coach to put a defeat behind him than to enjoy a victory.

“We coaches don’t enjoy victories because we immediately think about the next game. Defeat, however, stays with you. But what happened to me at Milan was incredibly emotional. Sackings, on the other hand, are difficult; you feel guilty.

“The one in Florence was even more difficult. I had returned with so much willpower and energy. I had returned with so much confidence, and it was a tough blow.”

Finally, a revelation about the possibility of becoming Italy’s coach. Pioli confirmed that he had been close to taking over the national team, but without going into details.

“I’ve touched on it, but not for very long. In our careers, we are the product of all the choices we make. Some are good, some aren’t.”
