#1802. Lisandro Martinez was stupid, selfish and let the club down: Man United fans may have loved 'The Butcher' but losing his head is the latest act on the road to a bitter Old Trafford exit, writes CHRIS WHEELER

Published: 22:00 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 22:00 EDT, 31 October 2026

To borrow a phrase from Lisandro Martinez, we expect more from him.

We expect more from a vastly experienced defender and World Cup winner. We expect more from a 28-year-old whose team-mates during a stellar career include Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo.

We expect more from Martinez than to fling an arm into the face of an opponent in the penalty box a matter of seconds after being booked for another offence with such a crucial game hanging in the balance.

How did he think he was going to get away with it? How did he think it was going to help Manchester United’s chances of staying out of the relegation zone or Michael Carrick’s prospects of keeping his job?

Just when Carrick needed cool heads among his senior players, Martinez went and lost his.

No sooner had his arm connected with Wesley Fofana than VAR official James Bell sent referee Peter Bankes to the monitor. A second yellow card followed and a penalty for Cole Palmer to convert Chelsea's second goal. Game over.

When Michael Carrick needed cool heads, Lisandro Martinez (right) went and lost his

He finds himself at the scene of the crime too often and his time at the club appears to be coming to an end

There was no way back for United from there, not in their current fragile state.

Carrick couldn’t say what he really thought of Martinez’s moment of madness, but legendary United goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel did it for him.

'I put this solely on Lisandro Martinez's shoulders,' fumed Schmeichel. 'This is an absolute disgrace how he played this game. The penalty, I have no words for how crazy that was. Then he walks off the pitch shaking his head like he's done nothing wrong. So bad.'

This is the same Martinez who landed himself with a club fine earlier this month for saying he expected more of United’s director of football Jason Wilcox in the transfer market last summer.

The same Martinez who scored a hapless own-goal down the road from Chelsea at Fulham in September. The same Martinez who turned his back on the ball against Tottenham a week earlier, and allowed Dominic Solanke to score a late equaliser at Old Trafford.

With his contract running out in June, and no sign of United intending to trigger a 12-month extension clause, it looks as though his time at United is coming to an end and not in the way he would have wanted.

‘Whatever the next Man United phase is, I think Martinez's time at the club has run its course,’ Joe Cole told TNT Sports. ‘In a Man United shirt, he's just at the scene of the crime too often.’

No doubt Martinez’s resentment over his contract situation played a part in his comment about Wilcox. While supporters have applauded him for calling out the club’s recruitment – and there is no doubt he has a point – his time would be better spent focussing on keeping the ball out of United’s net and keeping himself on the pitch rather than pointing the finger at others.

He has been one of United’s better signings of recent years, albeit one hampered by a succession of unfortunate injuries. The combative edge and winning mentality he brought from his time with Argentina and Ajax have been an asset to Erik ten Hag, Ruben Amorim and, to a lesser extent, Carrick.

Michael Carrick (left) could not say what he really thought but was let down by one of his more senior players

The fans love The Butcher and you can see why at a time when so many players who have passed through the doors during his five years at Old Trafford have failed to show enough heart for the fight

But this was a stupid, selfish act borne out of frustration which cost United any chance of winning this game and will keep Martinez out of United’s last fixture before the international break at home to Aston Villa next weekend.

By the time they return to action, there is no guarantee Carrick will still be in a job.

If you want to compare Michael Carrick’s successful spell in charge at United last season with the seemingly inexplicable drop-off this term, this was exactly the kind of marginal game that he was winning back then.

Think of Carrick’s first two matches in charge against Manchester City and Arsenal, and the 3-2 wins over Liverpool, Nottingham Forest and Fulham. Perhaps most relevant of all, the 1-0 win here over Chelsea in April when Matheus Cunha scored the only goal just before half-time.

If United had taken only half their chances in the first half at Stamford Bridge this time, they could have put the game to bed. Amad Diallo had enough of them to win it on his own.

It would be easy to say that Carrick’s luck has run out but it isn’t that easy in elite sport. The confidence that flowed through the team in those months between January and May has drained from his players. Chances are being missed, silly goals conceded. Experienced campaigners like Martinez are suffering from a rush of blood to the head, and every mistake is being punished. That’s what happens when the tide turns and you haven’t got the resilience to ride it out.

Every game looks hard for United at the moment. Their only victories this season have been at home to Sabah and Ipswich, and even the latter came with a slice of luck.

Who knows where their next win is coming from? As he left West London looking rather dazed, Carrick didn’t seem like a man who has the answer to that question.

It feels like Bruno Fernandes's great Manchester United career may be coming to an end

Once we knew Carrick would be in the dugout at Stamford Bridge, all the talk in the build-up to this game was about the return of captain Bruno Fernandes after he was dropped for last weekend’s defeat to Bournemouth.

Fernandes didn’t just come back into the line-up, he was back at No10 after vacating that role for Youri Tielemans in recent weeks. Tielemans was deservedly left on the bench here while Fernandes interchanged with Cunha in a fluid United attack that performed well in a promising first half.

But the Fernandes of old would have made his mark on this game. Got a goal or an assist to lead his team to victory and ram the taunts of rival fans down their throats.

But he did nothing of the sort. Too many passes went astray, too often the arms were thrown up in the air in frustration. When he had a great chance to put United ahead in the first half from Bryan Mbeumo’s brilliant pass, Fernandes blazed it over the bar.

One man can’t carry an entire team, but the Portugal star has come close to it at times during his seven-year career at Old Trafford. Here, though, was more evidence that his powers may be fading and this United team may be beyond help.

United were open to selling Fernandes to Al-Hilal last year and won’t break the bank to keep him when his current deal runs out in June. They might renew at the right price or at least trigger the 12-month option to make sure he doesn’t leave on a free transfer.

But it feels like a great United career may be coming to an end.

#1801. Goalkeeper involved in Jesus de Miguel death 'is suffering' after incident

FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono “is suffering” following the death of Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel, says team-mate Lautaro Spatz.

Owono collided with De Miguel during a Spanish second-tier game on Monday, which saw the forward suffer a cardiac arrest and later die in hospital.

Equatorial Guinea international Owono, 25, has since received racist abuse on social media, with his Instagram account subsequently deactivated.

Spatz, who was on the pitch when the incident happened, said the FC Andorra squad remained in shock.

"The entire FC Andorra squad has been in shock, devastated and deeply affected by what has happened,” he wrote on Instagram.

“It is a tragedy that we could never have imagined experiencing on a football pitch.

"I would also like to say a few words about my team-mate, goalkeeper and friend, who is deeply affected by what has happened.

"Those of us who know him are aware of the sort of person he is, how much he is suffering at this time, and that he would never have intended to harm anyone.

“In football, there are accidental incidents, but no one could have imagined that one of them could lead to such tragic consequences."

Spanish police have opened an investigation into De Miguel’s death, in accordance with procedures for deaths involving non-natural causes, including accidents.

Tenerife’s majority shareholder Rayco García confirmed the entire squad would travel to mainland Spain to attend De Miguel’s funeral in Navahermosa, Toledo, on Thursday.

García told El Larguero: "The important thing now is for the players to say goodbye to their teammate and come to terms with what has happened. It's a tragic situation. There are things that some of our players shouldn't have had to witness.

“A football pitch is a place where you're meant to have a good time, and what we saw was anything but that.

"We're still in shock. The entire squad is going to the funeral, without exception. Then we'll return to Tenerife. The players will have the day off to continue coming to terms with this terrible blow. And on Saturday, at the Heliodoro [stadium,] we plan to hold a lovely tribute in his memory.

"We want to start coming to terms with this as soon as possible and look to the future. We know that Jesús will be with us."

#1800. Sturm Graz vs Celje - prediction, team news, lineups

By Darren Plant | 03 Nov 2026 12:11

Sturm Graz play host to Celje in their fourth match of the league phase of the Europa League on Thursday night.

With these two teams having just one win between them so far, it could prove to be a pivotal fixture with regards to the final table in January.

Having missed out to Fenerbahce in Champions League qualification, Sturm Graz were presented with a brutal start to their Europa League campaign.

However, collecting four points from games against Rennes, Bournemouth and Marseille represents an excellent return as they bid to earn a spot in the top 24.

The 1-0 success over Marseille on matchday three has left Fabio Ingolitsch's side in 19th position in the league phase table.

Nevertheless, they have since posted successive draws in the Austrian Bundesliga to sit 11 points adrift of leaders Rapid Vienna.

With just five wins from 11 league contests, Ingolitsch will recognise that he needs a strong return on the continent to ensure that he keeps his job.

Meanwhile, opponents Celje find themselves down in fifth place in the Slovenian top flight.

That is despite a five-match unbeaten streak being put together across all competitions since October 18.

Included in that run is a 2-2 draw against Sturm Graz's domestic rivals Red Bull Salzburg, highlighting that Zoran Zeljkovic's side have the quality required to push their next opponents.

Since his appointment as head coach in September, he has only overseen defeats to Bayer Leverkusen, a day after his arrival, and Omonia.

Oumar Diakite came off the substitutes' bench to score Sturm Graz's equaliser at Wolfsberger AC last time out, and he could replace Belmin Beganovic down the centre of the attack.

Luis Balbo is also an option to come into the team at left wing-back, while Albert Vallci may be recalled in the back three.

Barring any fitness issues, Zeljkovic could name the same Celje XI from the 4-0 win over NK Nafta, who are in sixth place, on Sunday.

Mario Kvesic and Armandas Kucys both scored doubles in that contest, the latter finally ending his 10-game wait for a goal in this season's Slovenian top flight.

Attacking midfielder Svit Seslar is Celje's leading marksman with seven goals.

Although Sturm Graz have only scored one goal from three matches in this competition, we cannot ignore that their opponents have conceded seven. With that in mind, the Austrian giants get our backing to come through with a comfortable victory.

#1799. Man City XI vs RB Leipzig: Predicted lineup, confirmed team news, injury latest for Champions League today

Manchester City are nearly at full strength for tonight’s Champions League meeting with RB Leipzig.

Antoine Semenyo is Man City’s one long-term absentee after suffering a knee injury in the win over Ipswich last month, keeping him out of the last four matches across all competitions as a result.

The Ghana international, along with youngsters Ryan McAidoo and Kaden Braithwaite, was not spotted during Tuesday’s open training session before flying out to Germany, but Enzo Maresca still has a near complete squad to choose from.

There is, however, a decision to make in goal as Gianluigi Donnarumma has looked shaky in recent weeks and the City boss has made it clear that the Italian is not a guaranteed starter.

“I think it is one thing to say that in this moment it is Gigio [Donnarumma] plus 10, and another thing to say undroppable,” Maresca said before the loss to Brighton in the Premier League.

“They are two different things. There is no player that is undroppable but in this moment it is Gigio plus 10. In this moment I see it like this.”

Geronimo Rulli staked his claim for a start with an impressive display in the Carabao Cup win over Brighton but may have to settle for a place on the bench again.

Marc Guehi and Nico O’Reilly are pushing for returns after dropping down to the bench at the weekend, while Ayyoub Bouaddi could be rested after starting the last two games.

Phil Foden is highly likely to start as he was chosen for pre-match press conference duties, though he might be asked to operate from the right-hand side as Rayan Cherki is recalled in the No10 role behind Erling Haaland.

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Crystal Palace have failed with their appeal against Jean-Philippe Mateta’s red card against Tottenham.

The French striker will serve a three-match suspension following his early dismissal during Saturday’s 2-0 loss in north London.

By Matt Law | 03 Nov 2026 12:30, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 12:32

Alejandro Balde has reportedly 'accepted' that he needs to leave Barcelona during the January transfer window for the sake of his career.

An incredibly frustrating campaign has seen the Spain international feature for just 116 minutes in all competitions, and he did not start Barcelona's league game against Alaves on Saturday even though Xavi Espart, Jules Kounde, Andreas Christensen and Eric Garcia were all out.

Balde is down the pecking order when it comes to the left-back spot at Barcelona under Hansi Flick, and according to Mundo Deportivo, the 23-year-old has 'accepted' that he will need to leave in the winter window due to his current struggles.

The report claims that the full-back is 'attracted' to the idea of playing in the Premier League amid interest from Manchester United.

The 20-time English champions were heavily linked with Balde over the summer, but the defender made it clear that he was not interested in a departure.

The situation has now changed, and it is understood that Man United are preparing to reignite their interest in January given their struggles at left-back.

Patrick Dorgu has recently returned to action, but his best football in a Man United shirt has come as an advanced option down the left.

Luke Shaw is currently injured, while neither Diogo Dalot nor Noussair Mazraoui have been convincing for Man United on the left side of the defence.

Balde has made 172 appearances for Barcelona in all competitions since breaking into their first team in 2021, scoring three goals and registering 21 assists.

The Spaniard has played 31 times in the Champions League during his career, and not too long ago, was regarded as one of the best left-backs in world football.

However, most of the signs are pointing towards a January departure, and Man United now seemingly have the perfect chance to bring Balde to Old Trafford.

#1796. Who are Scott Parker's backroom team? West Ham legends reunite for new era

West Ham have announced the appointment of Scott Parker as their new head coach to replace Nuno Espirito Santo.

Parker quickly succeeds Nuno, who was sacked on Tuesday morning after West Ham’s 3-1 defeat by West Brom, as the Irons look to get their automatic promotion bid back on track.

The former West Ham midfielder is seen as a safe pair of hands given his knowledge of the club and vast previous experience in getting teams promoted from the Championship.

West Ham are currently eighth in the Championship table, having won six of their first 13 league games, and take on Cardiff on Wednesday night, with Parker set to be in the dugout.

The 46-year-old, who has been out of work since leaving Burnley in April following confirmation of their relegation from the Premier League, will be joined by first-team coaches Steve Potts, Gerard Prenderville and Billy Lepine, while Mark Noble will also be working closely with the squad.

The permanent structure of Parker’s backroom staff has yet to be announced, but Standard Sport has assessed who will assist the former England international during his first game at the helm in Wales.

A club legend and former team-mate of Parker’s, Noble became West Ham’s sporting director in January 2023 but now looks set for a more hands-on role within the backroom team.

A West Ham fan, Lepine was appointed head of academy goalkeeping in November 2020 before being promoted to Nuno’s backroom team.

He worked alongside Nuno’s long-time assistant, Rui Barbosa, as a goalkeeping coach and helped Mads Hermansen re-establish himself as the club’s first-choice option after he was dropped from the side under Graham Potter.

#1795. GdS: From a curse to a blessing – the factors behind Milan’s recent derby dominance

AC Milan won the derby again on Saturday night, continuing their recent dominance of the fixture, despite Inter celebrating more silverware.

La Gazzetta dello Sport write that Milan planted their flag in the middle of the Duomo and have not removed it for two years. Something strange is happening in the city, frankly inexplicable: Inter haven’t won in eight derbies, even though on paper they’re almost always the stronger team.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Since September 2024, the Nerazzurri have had eight matches against Milan, losing six and drawing too. But why does this keep happening? The paper have attempted to offer some explanations.

Between January 2023 and April 2024, Inter won six consecutive derbies. It became Stefano Pioli’s curse. Three matches were more difficult than the others: the two 2023 Champions League semi-finals and the April 2024 derby, in which Simone Inzaghi’s side sealed the Scudetto.

It was the pinnacle for Inter fans and the worst nightmare for Milan fans, not coincidentally commemorated last night by the Nord with its choreography. From that moment on, Milan turned things around.

In September 2024, they won with Matteo Gabbia’s 89th-minute header, and it all changed from there. A pair of draws, then the 3-0 Coppa Italia win with a Luka Jovic brace, the two 1-0 wins last season (Pulisic in the first leg, Estupinan in the return), and this 3-1 win most recently.

For the reasons, you should consult a psychologist, but some things can be understood. Milan certainly play much more freely than during those terrible 15 months.

They’re definitely finding tactical solutions they didn’t have in that run under Pioli, where they pressed hard and ended up only allowing counter-attacks. They especially struggled greatly against Dimarco, Calhanoglu, and Mkhitaryan.

Paulo Fonseca initiated the change, reinforced by Sergio Conceiçao in the Supercoppa Italiana final, by Massimiliano Allegri, and now by Amorim. Milan are increasingly confident and, as much as possible in a crazy situation like the derby, control the games.

This time, they struggled very little, even in the second half, as if they had the password to counter Inter’s moves. Much of it was a question of energy: Milan no longer fear their cousins, they go head-to-head, and often win the duels in recent derbies.

Then, of course, there are the individuals. Christian Pulisic is becoming a ghost for Inter, fitting of these times. CP11 has scored in four of the last eight derbies, and they’ve all been crucial goals. With his intelligence, he understands where to strike Inter. With his speed, he surprises them.

As for that intelligence thing, Luka Modric is second to none. In the derby that Pervis Estupinan won, he was the best on the field. In Saturday’s resounding win, he helped the team manage the tempo, defended up front, winning back valuable balls, and even left the free kick to Moreira.

Add Adrien Rabiot to the list of Inter nightmares: ‘the Duke’ has earned 7.5, 7, and 7.5 again in the three Milan derbies he has played (Gazzetta ratings). Throwing all that together, and you get a one-sided fixture.

#1793. Lillestrom vs Viktoria Plzen - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 03 Nov 2026 12:57, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 12:59

Two teams yet to get going in the league stage of the 2026-27 Europa League will lock horns on Thursday, as Lillestrom welcome Viktoria Plzen.

Lillestrom are currently 31st in the overall table, boasting one point from three matches, while Viktoria Plzen are down in 33rd on zero points.

Lillestrom got their 2026-27 Europa League league stage off to a disappointing note, losing 2-1 at home to Torreense, but they did manage to claim a point in their second match of the competition away to Sparta Prague in the middle of October.

Any momentum gained from the draw with Sparta Prague was taken away in their third game, though, having suffered a 6-0 home defeat to Real Sociedad last time out.

The Canaries have one point to show from their three matches, which has left them 31st in the overall table ahead of their final five fixtures in the league stage of this tournament against Viktoria Plzen, Lyon, Levski, Bournemouth and Celta Vigo.

Hans Erik Odegaard's side will enter this match off the back of a 1-0 win over Start in the Eliteserien, and they have actually been victorious in each of their last three games.

Lillestrom, who are five-time Swedish champions, won the Norwegian Cup last season to qualify for the Europa League as a second-tier outfit.

Viktoria Plzen have also found it difficult in this season's competition, losing all three of their matches to sit down in 33rd spot in the table on zero points.

Radoslav Kovac's side started their league stage with a 3-0 home defeat to Union SG, before going down 2-1 to Ferencvaros in their second match on October 15; the Czech outfit were then beaten 2-1 at home by Levski in their third match in this season's tournament.

Viktoria Plzen will enter this match off the back of successive wins, including a 4-0 victory over Ostava in the league on November 1.

The Czech outfit reached the knockout round playoffs in the 2025-26 Europa League and actually went unbeaten in the league stage, so it is a surprise to see them struggling towards the bottom of the table at this moment in time.

Lillestrom are set to be without the services of Vebjorn Hoff and Kristoffer Tonnessen through injury, but the home side are otherwise in good shape for the contest.

Felix Va has been in strong form this season, scoring 10 goals and registering five assists in 28 appearances, and the 28-year-old will continue in the final third of the field.

Thomas Lehne Olsen has seven goals in all competitions this season, and the 35-year-old is set to feature through the middle for the Swedish outfit.

Viktoria Plzen, meanwhile, will be without the services of Jan Paluska and Vaclav Jemelka through injury for the European fixture on Thursday night.

Christophe Kabongo is the team's leading goalscorer this season, finding the back of the net on seven occasions in 16 appearances, and the 23-year-old will feature through the middle.

Meanwhile, there is set to be a spot in the side for Amar Memic, who has come up with 10 goal contributions in all competitions this term, managing four goals and six assists.

#1792. Mikel Arteta has Max Dowman conundrum to solve as Arsenal face Prague battle

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Prague will always hold a special place in Max Dowman's heart.

Aged 15 years and 308 days old, Dowman came on at the Fortuna Arena last season and in doing so became the youngest player to feature in the Champions League.

UEFA have been kind enough to mark the anniversary. Exactly a year on from that fixture, Arsenal are back at the same stadium to face Slavia Prague once again.

It has been an eventful 12 months for Dowman, who now has a Premier League medal in his possession, but it has been a particularly dramatic week.

The 16-year-old has served the first match of a three-game suspension for the straight red card he was shown against Fleetwood.

That ban does not apply to European competitions. Dowman played a full part in training on Tuesday and is part of the travelling squad in Prague.

The decision for Mikel Arteta is whether to hand Dowman a first Champions League start, or continue a period of tough love.

In response to criticism of his reaction to Dowman at Fleetwood, when he angrily spoke to the teenager as he walked off the pitch, Arteta made it clear that no allowances would be made for Dowman because of his age.

“This is the environment and this is the reality,” Arteta said.

“Otherwise we are in Disneyland, we are not in Disneyland, we are in the Premier League at this level and we look after him so much that you cannot imagine.

“But at the same time we are going to demand him, like to anybody else, because he needs to earn the right to play.”

Dowman cannot play in the Premier League until Arsenal host Manchester City on November 29, but the Champions League offers the chance for him to move on from that red card.

It was the second time in a month that Dowman had been sent off, having also been dismissed for England's Under-19s.

Arteta has been very clear that he has hammered home the message to Dowman that he must expect rough treatment and, more importantly, that he cannot react.

Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal triple raid; Man Utd want Bellingham

Choose the right education path for your child

Those discussions will have continued since the Fleetwood red card and those thoughts will be front of Arteta's mind when he selects his lineup in Prague.

Before Tuesday night's fixtures in the Champions League, Slavia Prague ranked seventh out of the 36 teams in the competition for fouls committed. They are the only side to have been shown two red cards this season.

When the two teams met last season, the hosts committed 24 fouls. Dowman was barely on the pitch for 20 minutes and was fouled twice.

The approach Slavia Prague might adopt towards Dowman, then, is no great surprise. Particularly after his recent red cards, there will be a feeling that the teenager can be riled and will react to a physical test.

However, Arsenal are not flush with options. Bukayo Saka is out with a quad injury and Noni Madueke just about shook off an ankle issue in time to play the full 90 minutes at Anfield.

With Saka out, Madueke is a pivotal part of Arsenal's attack and they cannot afford for him to be injured. Dowman is now unable to ease the domestic load but he can allow Madueke a precious rest on Wednesday night.

Ordinarily, that would feel like a fairly obvious call for Arteta to make. The past week has perhaps complicated the situation and given Arteta more to ponder.

Does he leave Dowman on the bench, whether it be to send him a message or to protect him considering the current spotlight? Or does he show his faith in the teenager and trust him to learn the necessary lessons to keep a cooler head?

Arteta indicated at his pre-match press conference that he will opt for the latter and put the Fleetwood saga in the past.

“That’s a chapter that is gone,” Arteta said.

“It’s a moment of learning for all of us and we move on. You learn from the not so good ones, make sure you learn from the great ones as well. He’s been in great spirits.”

Against limited opposition and on a night where rotation is likely, it feels an ideal opportunity for Arteta to showcase his trust and Dowman to repay it.

#1791. Wesley Fofana has a shot at redemption after shocking first half in Man United win, Estevao cements his status as Chelsea's fan favourite - and why Romeo Lavia was their star man, writes KIERAN GILL

Published: 02:01 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 04:27 EDT, 1 November 2026

There is something called the Science of Scare Project.

It is a study ranking the most frightening films of all time by measuring an audience’s reaction to watching them. Via their average heart rate, highest spike, time between heartbeats, and so on.

Halloween enthusiasts consulting this year’s eerie list found the spookiest ever was a 2012 supernatural horror called Sinister. That received a 'Scare Score' of 96/100. It beat The Conjuring (88/100), Paranormal Activity (73/100), Texas Chainsaw Massacre (65/100), and so on.

If only the good folks behind this scientific study had hooked up the Chelsea fans at Stamford Bridge. It would have been intriguing to know the fluctuating activity of their hearts as they watched Wesley Fofana flirt with gifting Manchester United the opening goal.

We would have seen the spikes occur whenever he was involved. Chelsea’s major mistakes came from the 25-year-old Frenchman, who will be needed more while Maxence Lacroix is recovering from his hamstring injury.

Xabi Alonso has told us Lacroix is facing ‘a few weeks’ on the sidelines, but sources around the player have suggested he may not return until 2027. That information has also been stood up by the odd contact at the club.

Chelsea’s major mistakes came from the 25-year-old Frenchman, who will be needed more

Chelsea supporters were thrilled they got to watch Estevao (left) and now he has given Alonso a selection headache

Which is worrying for Alonso and Co. While Chelsea wound up winning 2-0 against an abysmal United team now hovering over the relegation zone, Fofana’s first half was a shocker.

First, he was burgled of the ball by the halfway line. Amad countered, and while he should have made more of the chance, he won a corner. United scored from this attacking phase, but Chelsea survived when VAR decided the scorer, Matheus Cunha, was offside.

Then, Fofana misjudged a long pass to leave Amad with only Mike Penders to beat. Chelsea got away with that one, too.

This followed what happened at Anfield on Wednesday when Chelsea exited the Carabao Cup. Fofana swapped football for volleyball at a Liverpool corner to hand them their penalty equaliser. At the shootout, he was the unfortunate soul who skied the decisive spot-kick to confirm defeat.

If Alonso had any other senior central defenders available on his bench, he might have made the change at half-time versus United. He did not, and so Fofana survived a hooking.

To Fofana’s credit, he calmed after the break. He was the one clattered to win Chelsea their penalty and earn Lisandro Martinez his second yellow. There was even a point towards the end, when Chelsea were leading 2-0 against United’s 10 men, that he was trying to pass from the back.

Bruno Fernandes stood in his way and so he simply nutmegged his opponent to find Valentin Barco. As Fofana jogged by Fernandes immediately afterwards, he rubbed it in a little, laughing at United’s captain with a little finger-wagging gesture.

That told us the confidence is there, though Chelsea fans will continue to fear he is a player too prone to a clanger, rather than a centre back who cost £75million from Leicester City in 2022.

Even before his errors here, there were pieces penned by other websites suggesting he should be seen as the worst signing of the BlueCo era. Thanks to his driving infringements, we know how much he earns, too. More than £200,000 per week, his lawyer had to tell Lavender Hill Magistrates' Court in January as his client reached a remarkable 50 points on his licence.

It is fair to say he has not lived up to the hype which accompanied his arrival with injuries having hampered his career. But here is a small chance at redemption. Lacroix may miss the remainder of 2026, and Fofana will be needed. Chelsea would love him to reduce his 'Scare Score' which, in the first half of this win over United, was rivalling Sinister’s record.

Those of us inside Stamford Bridge did not notice it. We thought Bryan Mbeumo had sent his shot straight into the crossbar. But then we saw Penders celebrating, and the slow-mo replays.

Penders got his fingertips to it. He stopped any chance it had of creeping underneath the crossbar to reduce the scoreline to 2-1. The 21-year-old Belgian earned this clean sheet.

It was good to see. He had a nightmare against Tottenham, there is no hiding from that. He punched a cross into his own goal to give Spurs their opener in that 2-0 defeat. But at Liverpool in the Carabao Cup, he responded well. Then here against United, he would not be beaten.

There has been talk of Chelsea rushing back Martinez from his jaw injury, maybe by having him wear a protective mask. But Penders performing like this may mean that is not necessary.

The loudest cheer when the line-ups were announced was reserved for Estevao, followed by Stamford Bridge chanting ‘Stevo, Stevo’. They love him, and they are right to love him.

He had to wait a long time for his first Premier League start of the season. Arguably too long.

But he seized his opportunity. Estevao scored two goals – alas, both were disallowed for offside – but he was forever involved. Chelsea supporters were thrilled they got to watch him, and now, he has given Alonso a selection headache because it was a showing which said he should start more.

Daily Mail Sport reported in our Chelsea Confidential column this week how there had been no fallout between Alonso and Estevao, despite speculation suggesting otherwise. His exclusion from the line-up was down to tactical and technical decisions.

When Estevao thought he had scored for the second time, he ran over to Alonso to give him a hug. When substituted, there was another cuddle. All is fine in that relationship, even if the 19-year-old Brazilian is itching to play more.

Lavia was actually the best performer in this victory. It was his winning of the ball that led to Rogers scoring

Jordan Henderson fell ill and so was unable to start his sixth successive match for Chelsea.

By Matt Law | 03 Nov 2026 13:29, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 13:31

The Anoeta Stadium will play host to a fascinating Europa League contest on Thursday, as Real Sociedad welcome Lyon in the league stage of the tournament.

Real Sociedad are currently 14th in the overall table, picking up four points from three matches, while Lyon are 12th, collecting six points from three games.

Real Sociedad were outstanding in their last Europa League fixture on October 22, recording a 6-0 victory over Lillestrom, with that result following a 2-1 home loss to Bournemouth and a 1-1 draw with Union SG in this season's league stage.

Four points from three games has left them in 14th spot in the division, and they have matches after this one against Crystal Palace, Torreense, Viktoria Plzen and Juventus.

Pellegrino Matarazzo's side will enter this match off the back of a 2-1 defeat to Athletic Bilbao in the Basque derby, so they will be fired-up to bounce back on Thursday.

The White and Sky Blues reached the last-16 stage of the Europa League in their last participation in the tournament in 2024-25, and it would be a surprise if they were unable to advance deep into this season's competition given their quality.

Real Sociedad have won three of their last four matches in all competitions, while their loss in the Basque derby on Sunday was their first defeat of any kind since September 17.

Lyon, meanwhile, will enter this match off the back of a 2-0 win over Angers in Ligue 1, with that result following back-to-back defeats for the French club.

One of those losses came in the team's last European fixture, going down 3-0 against Hoffenheim on October 22, with that result coming after a 3-2 success over Crystal Palace.

Paulo Fonseca's side also won their opening match in this season's Europa League league stage, beating Anderlecht 2-1, so six points have been gathered from three matches, which has left them in 12th spot in the division ahead of the next round of fixtures.

Lyon reached the last-16 stage of the 2025-26 Europa League, going out of the competition to Celta Vigo, while they made the quarter-finals in 2024-25, losing to Manchester United.

Les Gones will also take on Lillestrom, Union SG, Jagiellonia and Bayer Leverkusen before the league stage of the Europa League draws to a close.

Real Sociedad will be without the services of Luken Beitia, Alvaro Odriozola and Arsen Zakharyan through injury on Thursday night.

Luka Sucic is actually the team's leading goalscorer this season, coming up with six goals in 13 appearances, and he is set to continue in the final third of the field.

Meanwhile, there will be a start in the attack for Spain's World Cup winner Mikel Oyarzabal.

As for Lyon, Nicolas Tagliafico, Mohamed Ouedraogo, Tyler Morton, Pavel Sulc and Lois Openda are out of the European fixture due to injury problems.

Noah Nartey has been a standout performer for Lyon this season, coming up with two goals from midfield, and the 21-year-old will be in the starting side.

There is also expected to be a spot in an attacking area for Keito Nakamura.

#1786. Jesus de Miguel: Kylian Mbappe, Pedri lead tributes to Tenerife striker following death aged 30

By Ben Knapton | 03 Nov 2026 13:49

The footballing world was rocked by unimaginable tragedy on November 3, when Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel Alameda died at the age of 30 following a collision with an opposing goalkeeper.

De Miguel and FC Andorra shot-stopper Jesus Owono both charged down a long ball towards the end of a Segunda Division match on Monday, and the latter's knee collided with the former's face and chest.

Distressed players from both teams immediately called for medical attention, and De Miguel was immediately taken to hospital, where his condition was reported as serious but stable.

However, De Miguel devastatingly deteriorated overnight, and the forward lost his life in the early hours of Tuesday morning following a cardiac arrest.

De Miguel's death sparked an outpouring of tributes from across the globe, as players, clubs, organisations, member associations and high-ranking officials all offered their support to the late striker, his family, his friends and his club.

Rotos de dolor, con un nudo en la garganta y sin poder creer que esto sea verdad, desde el CD Tenerife comunicamos el trágico fallecimiento, este martes, día 3 de noviembre de 2026, a las 8:00 horas, de Jesús de Miguel Alameda. No hay palabras de consuelo; no hay absolutamente nada que mitigue este sentimiento repleto de tristeza. Estamos junto a su desolada familia, junto a sus seres queridos, junto a todo el tinerfeñismo que hoy llora por este cruel desenlace. La familia de Jesús de Miguel agradece todas y cada una de las muestras de apoyo recibidas, e igualmente solicita, de corazón, máximo respeto a su privacidad, en estos terribles momentos. ? DEP

Meanwhile, Barcelona midfielder Pedri wrote on social media: "The death of Jesus de Miguel leaves me speechless. A huge hug for his family and the Tenerife family. And a heartfelt and respectful remembrance for him. Rest in peace."

Ex-Barcelona, Chelsea and Spain winger Pedro described De Miguel's loss as "irreplaceable", saying: "Deeply saddened by the passing of Jesús. All my love and affection to his family and friends for this irreplaceable loss. A big hug to everyone in Tenerife."

La Liga president Javier Tebas reposted Tenerife's original statement on X, saying: "Deeply saddened by the passing of Jesus de Miguel Alameda, player of CD Tenerife.

"Today we all share the terrible pain of an irreparable loss. My deepest condolences to his family, loved ones, teammates, and his entire club. All my affection and support in these such difficult moments. Rest in peace."

Fulham head coach Alvaro Arbeloa also expressed his condolences, saying: ""All my affection and my deepest condolences to the family of Jesus, to his loved ones, and to all of tinerfenismo. Rest in peace."

Among those to reply to Tenerife's social media statement were David de Gea, who posted a broken heart and prayer emoji, and Gerard Pique, who wrote "I am sorry with all my soul. Rest in peace, Jesus."

Real Madrid defender Eder Militao responded: "Sad day for football. Strength to all their family and friends", while Aymeric Laporte wrote "DEP" for descanse en paz, which translates to rest in peace.

Formerly of the Leganes youth academy, De Miguel exclusively spent his professional career in the lower leagues of Spanish football, as well as making a handful of Copa del Rey appearances.

The 1996-born striker moved to Tenerife in the summer of 2025 and was a key player in their successful promotion bid from the third tier in 2025-26, scoring 11 goals and providing seven assists in 29 league matches.

Miguel had previously represented Castellon in the Segunda Division and also played for Unionistas CF, CDA Navalcarnero, CF Fuenlabrada, AD Union Adarve and Internacional de Madrid.

#1785. Santos impresses in first Man Utd appearance but cannot prevent defeat by Wrexham

Andrey Santos made a bright first Manchester United appearance as they fell to a pre-season friendly loss to Wrexham in Helsinki.

Sam Smith scored the only goal with an easy finish six minutes before half-time, moments after heading against his own crossbar defending a corner.

United were without the players who have featured at this summer’s World Cup – including new signing Youri Tielemans – as well as Benjamin Sesko, but Michael Carrick put out a strong starting XI in front of 20,000 spectators in the Finnish capital.

Santos, who became United’s first summer signing when he joined from Chelsea at the start of the week for an initial £48m, took his place at the base of midfield alongside Mason Mount.

Speaking just before the match, Michael Carrick had praised the 22-year-old’s attitude, saying: “He’s settled in really well, he’s a fantastic character. He’s buzzing to be here, you can see that.”

The Brazilian’s first involvement was to clear the ball away after Tom Heaton failed to gather under pressure from Smith seconds into the game.

Santos was left on his backside by Lewis O’Brien eight minutes in but the chance came to nothing for Wrexham as the flag went up. More encouraging was his sliding block on O’Brien moments later and he soon settled in, showing a good range of passing and winning several duels in a busy display.

However, Phil Parkinson’s side, who played their first pre-season friendly against Wisla Krakow in Poland last weekend, were looking brighter and threatened again when Bailey Cadamarteri nicked the ball off Ayden Heaven on the edge of the box before the defender recovered.

United’s first chance was a Joshua Zirkzee shot that fizzed wide in the 24th minute and they almost went ahead when Smith tried to clear a cornerm but instead sent a header on to his own crossbar in the 36th minute.

Moments later Smith was on the scoresheet at the other end and it looked all too easy as he was left with a tap-in after O’Brien’s cross appeared to go through Harry Maguire’s legs.

Sam Smith with the winning moment 🤌🔴⚪️#WxmAFC pic.twitter.com/YzTvnzIpz6

Twenty-one of the 22 players were replaced at half-time, with only Wrexham’s Aaron James staying on, and Carrick sent out a side entirely composed of academy products, facing a decent test against a Wrexham side now including the likes of Conor Coady and Kieffer Moore.

United dominated the ball but struggled to fashion chances as the pace of the game dropped. Instead, Wrexham threatened with a low shot from Davis Keillor-Dunn but Radek Vitek made the save.

When Ethan Wheatley prodded Harry Amass’ cross goalwards in the 78th minute, it was their first shot on target, but Dan Ward made the save before holding a low drive from Shea Lacey.

Dan Gore hit the deck in the single minute of stoppage time, but his optimistic penalty appeal was waved away.

We knew it wouldn’t be perfect - that’s only natural for the first pre-season game - and the main thing is that everybody came through it in good shape. No injuries so we can move onto the next step next week.

[Andrey Santos] and Mason [Mount] did some really good things and connected really well. There’s loads of little positives to take. The sharpness at the top end will come as we move through pre-season.

I was really pleased with the second half team. They controlled the game really well against a team who aren’t easy to play against. The boys took responsibility and their quality; they can really be proud of themselves.

Man Utd appeal unsuccessfully for a penalty when Dan Gore goes over in the area. Seconds later, the referee blows the final whistle. Wrexham, who were under pressure for much of the second half, have held on to beat Manchester United in a muted pre-season friendly in Helsinki.

Sam Smith scored the only goal in the 39th minute, having headed against his own crossbar three minutes earlier. There were 21 changes at half-time, 11 for Man Utd and 10 for Wrexham.

Andrey Santos, part of an experienced first-half XI, had a decent debut after signing from Chelsea in the week. The senior players looked understandably rusty, and a very youthful replacement XI were more dominant than their seniors. But they struggled to create clear chances and Wrexham deserved their win.

Full-time in Helsinki 🇫🇮First pre-season minutes in the tank for 22 Reds ✔️

Wheatley finds the underlapping Amass, whose pullback is cleared a little desperately by Wrexham. Amass, still only 19, looks really promising at left-back.

Man Utd’s youngsters continue to press for an equaliser. They haven’t created much but the rest of their second-half performance has been impressive.

Ward makes another comfortable save, this time when Shea Lacey tries his luck from 22 yards.

The left-back Harry Amass beats his man and curls a cross that bounces towards Ethan Wheatley at the near post. He stabs it goalwards and Ward makes a comfortable save. Tough chance, though Wheatley did well to get across the defender.

Man Utd’s best move of the second half. Dan Gore runs onto a return pass from Shea Lacey and sweeps a low ball into the six-yard box that is held at the second attempt by Danny Ward.

Wrexham substitution Alex Moore replaces Aaron James, who was the only starter on either side to play part of the second half.

The first chance of the second half falls to Wrexham. After a neat move through midfield, Davis Keillor-Dunn gallops into the area and drives a low shot that Radek Vitek saves well with his legs.

Kamason is booked for a late tackle on Dobson. That looked a bit harsh, certainly in a friendly.

Wrexham - in a back five, heaven forfend - are defending well and keeping the opposition at arm’s length. Unlike Argentina, Man Utd haven’t really tried any crosses yet.

No attempts at goal in the second half, on or off target, from either team. But the young Man Utd side have played some purposeful stuff and have had around 66% possession.

No chances to report but the young Man Utd side have started well, dominating possession and playing with greater urgency than their elders.

And this is the youthful XI that Michael Carrick has put out for the second half.

Man Utd (4-2-3-1) Vitek; Kamason, Devaney, Armer, Amass; Collyer, T Fletcher; Lacey, Gore, Williams; Wheatley.

Wrexham have made 10 changes, with Aaron James the only survivor from the first half. This is their new XI.

Our second-half XI 👇🔴⚪ #WxmAFC pic.twitter.com/pechlNMwxJ

Manchester United begin the second half having made 11 changes at half-time. We’ll have the full teams shortly, all being well.

Wrexham lead after a low-key first half in Helsinki. Sam Smith scored to enliven a half of few chances. Andrey Santos was lively on his Manchester United debut, gobbling up the ground defensively and playing forward at every opportunity.

We should have very different teams - perhaps completely new XIs - for the second half.

39 min: Man Utd 0 Wrexham 1 (Smith) Sam Smith gives Wrexham the lead. It came from a well-worked throw-in on the left. Thomason played a one-two before slipping a crisp pass into O’Brien in the area. His precise low cross, through the legs of Maguire, gave Smith a tap-in from three yards.

Man Utd hit the bar Mason Mount’s inswinging corner from the left is headed against his own crossbar by Sam Smith, woh was off balance as he challenged Leny Yoro. That’s the closest we’ve come to a goal at either end.

Broadhead wriggles away from Andrey Santos on the edge of the area, but Santos snaps back at him and Broadhead curls over the bar.

Zirkzee pulls up gingerly after being caught by a Wrexham player. Looks like an in impact injury rather than a muscle problem.

Santos and Mount probe on the edge of the Wrexham area. A through ball is cut out and rebounds towards Zirkzee, who whistles a snapshot wide from 20 yards. Not a bad effort.

Patrick Dorgu’s shot is blocked on the edge of the area. United are starting to find a bit of rhythm after a slow start.

Cadamarteri surges into the area and is about to shoot when Heaven makes an excellent lunging challenge. Wrexham look more likely to score at this point.

Smith barges Andrey Santos over long after the ball has gone. A bit of a needless challenge, one that Santos did not especially appreciate.

Both teams look rusty, United in particular. Wrexham have been a bit more direct and slightly more dangerous in attack.

Andrey Santos loses the ball in midfield, leading to a one-on-one chance for Sam Smith that is well saved by Heaten. Smith was offside so it wouldn’t have counted.

That opportunity aside, it’s been a predictably quiet start - lots of passing in midfield from United in particular.

The new signing Andrey Santos makes an important interception after 40 seconds. Nathan Broadhead seemed to foul the keeper Tom Heaton in the United area, but play continued and Broadhead’s ball across was turned behind by Santos.

Wrexham, in their blue change strip, kick off from right to left as we watch.

Both teams line up for the usual pre-match formalities. Harry Maguire and Matty James, a former Man Utd academy player, are the captains.

We’ve been back in training 10 days and we’re taking it step by step. It’s great to be back at it again.

Andrey Santos is a fantastic character and he’s settled in really well. He’s buzzing to be here and he’ll do really well for us. We’re not expecting anything crazy special today - it’s a step, just get your eye in and get back on the pitch. I’m really looking forward to the progression he shows while he’s here.

Youri Tielemans is targeting more silverware after completing his £35m move to Manchester United.

Tielemans has signed a five-year contract at Old Trafford after United triggered his release clause at Aston Villa.

The Belgium international played a key role in helping Villa lift the Europa League last season, but pushed for the move to United after turning down the offer of a new contract in the West Midlands.

“The ambition from everyone at the club is extremely clear; we are all determined to push for the biggest trophies,” he said.

“Signing for such a special club feels incredible, it is the culmination of years of dedication since I first fell in love with football. I have had the privilege of experiencing success in the game and it has only increased my determination to achieve more.”

I’m not sure when Man Utd last played Wrexham in a friendly, but the most recent competitive meeting between the sides was in January 1995. It was three days after Eric Cantona tried to kick xenophobia out of football at Selhurst Park, so United’s 5-2 win was somewhat overshadowed.

Andrey Santos starts in what is a pretty strong United XI.

Lining up for our first fixture of pre-season! 🇫🇮Watch LIVE on MUTV ⤵️

Our first-half XI in Helsinki 🇫🇮🔴⚪ #WxmAFC pic.twitter.com/WrXbc2B7JQ

The World Cup final? Pah! The 2026-27 Premier League season is just over a month away, and Manchester United’s pre-season begins this afternoon with a friendly against Wrexham in Helsinki.

Man Utd have started many seasons with a whimper since Sir Alex Ferguson’s retirement 13 years ago, but there’s plenty of summer optimism around Old Trafford. Michael Carrick overachieved so spectacularly as caretaker manager that a full-time appointment became inevitable. Now all he has to do is maintain that league form across a full season while also juggling the Champions League.

United have filled part of their midfield void by signing Andrey Santos from Chelsea and Youri Tielemans from Aston Villa. Tielemans is having a post-World Cup break but Santos is part of a United squad that also includes Bryan Mbeumo, Harry Maguire, Luke Shaw, Mason Mount, Patrick Dorgu and Leny Yoro.

“Everything about Manchester United is special,” said Santos after signing for the club earlier in the week. “It is an incredible feeling to join a club that some of my biggest idols have represented. As a midfielder, I am really excited to have the opportunity to learn from Michael Carrick. He is the perfect coach to help me take the next step in my career and push to achieve my dreams.”

If you include the loan and youth players, Liverpoolai??i??s squad strength is pretty massive. In the summer windows, one can look at options beyond these two. #1779. FIFA Slaps Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid With 1-Year Transfer Bans

Home » Home 2 » FIFA Slaps Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid With 1-Year Transfer Bans

The ban will start from the July transfer window this year and finish with the January transfer market in 2017.

Atletico were also fined 900,000 Swiss francs (820,000 euros) and Real 360,000 (330,000 euros).

“The two clubs were found to have violated several provisions concerning the international transfer and first registration of minor players as well as other relevant provisions with regard to the registration and participation of certain players in competitions,” said a FIFA statement.

Barcelona has just ended a one year ban for similar reasons.

Real and Atletico were “issued with a reprimand and given 90 days in which to regularise the situation of all minor players concerned,” FIFA said. They can still sell players during the transfer ban.

FIFA said the alarm was raised over the two clubs by FIFA’s Transfer Matching System and its disciplinary committee completed the inquiry.

Under international football rules, players under 18 cannot be transferred to another country, except in limited circumstances. All transfers need the approval of a special FIFA committee.

“The investigations concerned minor players who were involved and participated in competitions with the clubs over various periods between 2007 and 2014 (Atletico Madrid) and between 2005 and 2014 (Real Madrid),” FIFA said.

The ban follows a similar sanction handed to European champions Barcelona, who were unable to register new players during 2015.

Barca were initially banned in April 2014, but managed to delay the sanction taking affect until the transfer windows in January and the summer 2015 by launching an ultimately unsuccessful appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS).

By delaying the ban, Barca managed to sign the likes of Luis Suarez and Ivan Rakitic in the summer of 2014 to propel them to a treble of La Liga, Champions League and Copa del Rey.

The news is just the latest institutional embarassment for Real Madrid just over a week after they appointed French legend Zinedine Zidane.

Madrid have sacked two Champions League winning coaches in Carlo Ancelotti and Rafael Benitez in the past seven months, as well as being thrown out of the Copa del Rey for fielding an ineligible player.

The sanction could also be bad news for the likes of Paris Saint-Germain and Manchester United, who had targeted Madrid stars Cristiano Ronaldo and Gareth Bale with Real highly unlikely to dispose of their best players without the chance to sign suitable replacements.

La Liga leaders Atletico Madrid’s usually hectic transfer policy will also be put on hold. However, Diego Simeone’s men look better placed to cope with the ban having invested heavily in young talent over the past year.

Neither Real no Atletico made an immediate comment on whether they would appeal.

#1778. AC Milan vs Ferencvaros - prediction, team news, lineups

One of five teams still with maximum points in the Europa League, Hungarian giants Ferencvaros will put that perfect record on the line when they visit AC Milan on Thursday.

Though Milan celebrated a domestic derby win at San Siro last time out, they are at risk of making an early exit from Europe.

Seven-time European champions, Milan were humbled by modest Bournemouth in their last Europa League match, falling behind within a few minutes before seeing their captain sent off.

Without Mike Maignan, the Rossoneri went on to lose 3-0 on England's south coast, leaving them on three points from as many league-phase games.

Ruben Amorim had started with defeat to his old club Benfica, before recording a 4-0 victory in Salzburg, so his side certainly have some work left if they are to qualify for the knockout rounds.

It has been an eventful fortnight since Milan were picked off by the Cherries: first, they beat free-falling Udinese 2-0, then they suffered another midweek meltdown.

Amorim's unbeaten domestic record finally ended in a chaotic encounter at San Siro, which finished 4-2 to Bologna, and that was far from ideal preparation for the Derby della Madonnina.

Yet, the rampant Rossoneri surged into a two-goal lead over Inter on Saturday night, before their old foes pulled one back; then, as half time approached, Diego Moreira's stunning free-kick essentially put the result beyond doubt.

So, having closed within four points of their city rivals, Milan sit fifth in Serie A and are still in what could be a multi-club title race.

While Milan lie 24th in the Europa League table - occupying the final playoff place as things stand - Ferencvaros may be eyeing automatic entry to the last 16.

Hungary's most successful club currently sit fourth with maximum points, following a home win over Portuguese second-tier side Torreense last month.

Though they were level at half time, second-half strikes from Mariano Gomez and Krisztian Lisztes - scored either side of an own goal - saw Fradi stroll to a 4-1 victory.

After previously beating Celtic and Viktoria Plzen, Balazs Borbely's men are very much in contention to make the top eight, which would help them skip the precarious playoff round.

Incidentally, the last time Ferencvaros won four consecutive matches in major UEFA competition was way back in the 1967-68 campaign, when they posted six straight wins en route to the Inter-Cities Fairs Cup final.

Given recent results, Borbely's squad might hope to emulate that run: including all domestic games and four rounds of Europa League qualifying, they have only lost once this season.

Sunday's 2-0 victory over Paks left them just two points behind Hungarian league leaders - and reigning champions - ETO Gyor, but Fradi have one game in hand.

After the Milan derby and before Sunday's trip to Genoa, Amorim is set to rotate his squad, with players such as Alphadjo Cisse being promoted from the bench.

The young forward - who scored a hat-trick versus Salzburg and a brace against Bologna - could join Omari Hutchinson and Davide Bartesaghi in a reshuffled lineup.

As Maignan must serve a suspension for his red card against Bournemouth, Lorenzo Torriani should deputise in goal.

Injured quintet Fikayo Tomori, Samuel Chukwueze, Mattia Gabbia, Alexis Saelemaekers and Ruben Loftus-Cheek are still unavailable, while Filippo Terracciano remains a doubt.

Ferencvaros will be missing Slovakia midfielder Matus Bero, and Bence Otvos has yet to complete his recovery from an ACL injury.

Up front, Kristoffer Zachariassen (three goals, one assist) and Dele Yusuf (two goals, two assists) both aim to extend a fine start to the league phase.

The pair also notched one goal apiece last weekend; Serbian winger Veljko Birmancevic should join them in the final third.

His success came off the back of a stunning year with Bayern and England, with the forward netting a staggering 73 goals during the 2025-26 season.

Kane's goals spearheaded the German side's domestic Treble, while he also captained his country to third place at the World Cup.

And, ahead of Bayern's clash against Borussia Dortmund on Saturday night, Kane received a special presentation at the Allianz Arena.

Harry Kane presented his Ballon d'Or trophy to Bayern Munich fans and players on Saturday

#1771. EPL Prepares for Most Exciting Title Race in Years

Home » Home 2 » EPL Prepares for Most Exciting Title Race in Years

Now that all of the top four English Premier League teams have had a chance to play each other, we find ourselves looking at one of the most wide open title races in recent memory. As of this writing, the league leaders are only separated by a mere six points. With the exception of Manchester City, we could very well see a new face hoisting the Premier League trophy at the end of the season.

For much of the year, it looked like Arsenal would be in the running for its first league title in more than a decade. With the Gunners’ recent victory against Leicester City, they are very much back in the conversation. Danny Welbeck returned to the pitch for the first time this season and made an immediate impact for Arsene Wenger’s squad, scoring the last-minute, game-winning goal to propel the team to within two points of the top spot. Given that even more key players are set to return to action for Arsenal in the coming months, this is easily the best shot they have had of winning a championship since their undefeated 2003-04 season.

Another surprise team that certainly deserves its own mention is Tottenham Hotspur. Following the club’s controversial defeat of Manchester City, the Spurs sit in second place, a mere two points behind Leicester City and ahead of Arsenal on goal differential. Tottenham have yet to win a title in the Premier League era and they have not won an English championship since 1961. The team has done a superb job of backing up star striker Harry Kane with a glut of promising young players, and their goal tally only helps to reinforce the wisdom behind the strategy of manager Mauricio Pochettino.

Meanwhile, Manchester City is still hoping to snag its third title as something of a swan song for exiting manager Manuel Pellegrini. It was recently announced that the club had hired Pep Guardiola . from Bayern Munich to take charge of the team beginning with next season. Thus, Pellegrini has been forced to endure the rest of the campaign as a dead man walking. Despite the impending exit of Pellegrini, City are still in the race for the Premier League title in addition to both the F.A. Cup and Champions League. Theoretically, the club could pull off a treble, if it can manage a solid string of performances during the final half of the season.

At the beginning of the season, it was expected that the usual suspects would once again dominate the league. Many predicted the reigning champs at Chelsea to repeat their success. However, a shocking season has seen the team part ways with controversial manager Jose Mourinho and struggle to remain in the top half of the tables with hopes of a Champions League spot dashed long ago.

For the first time in years, there’s a chance to see a completely new team win the league. No matter which club you support, there’s no denying that this has made for one of the most thrilling contests in recent memory. In a league where money talks, small fish like Leicester City are surprising everyone, and we can only hope that this means a new era of parity for the Premier League.

Parker will inherit a squad that has undergone significant changes since relegation, with around £150m raised through player sales and some of that money reinvested in new arrivals.

However, the Hammers still have weaknesses to address, particularly in attack, and January could provide the new head coach with an opportunity to reshape his squad.

Sports Mole takes a look at three realistic names who could be among Parker's first signings in east London.

A striker should be near the top of Parker's shopping list, with Pablo and Taty Castellanos managing just two league goals between them in West Ham's opening 13 matches. Their combined six goal contributions are hardly convincing, particularly when centre-back Konstantinos Mavropanos has scored five times himself.

Abraham could offer a much-needed alternative, having struggled to secure regular opportunities since returning to Villa Park for around £18m in the summer. The 11-time England international also has an impressive Championship record, finding the net 48 times in 78 appearances at that level.

Another area requiring attention is the wide positions, particularly with Parker likely to favour his preferred 4-2-3-1 system. Manor Solomon has arrived to provide an attacking threat, but additional competition could help West Ham become more dangerous from the flanks.

Sancho remains without a club after leaving Manchester United in the summer, and the Irons have been linked with the former Borussia Dortmund star for several months. Reports suggest his representatives have contacted several English clubs, including the Hammers, to explore potential opportunities.

His Premier League record of 12 goals and 13 assists in 112 appearances is hardly spectacular, and there would understandably be reservations about taking a gamble on him. However, with no transfer fee required, Sancho could be a relatively low-cost opportunity for Parker to revive a player who has previously demonstrated considerable ability.

West Ham may also need to strengthen at centre-back, particularly with Mavropanos attracting reported interest from Turkish giants Besiktas following an encouraging start to the campaign.

Losing the Greece international would be a significant setback, especially given his importance to the defence, but it could force Parker to revisit an existing target. Rav van den Berg has been linked with the Hammers in recent windows, having cost FC Koln around £11m in 2025.

Parker would have encountered the former Middlesbrough defender during his time managing Burnley in the Championship, potentially giving him a useful understanding of his qualities.

With youngster Airidas Golambeckis already being asked to step into the first team, another centre-back would make sense even if Mavropanos stays.

A January move could therefore address a potential departure while adding a young defender with Championship experience.

#1767. The Rock of London: Looking back at John Terry’s Chelsea FC career

Home » Home 2 » The Rock of London: Looking back at John Terry’s Chelsea FC career

At the start of this season, John Terry leaving Chelsea was the last thing on anyone’s mind. All was rosy at Stamford Bridge, the home of the newly crowed English champions. In over 21 years at the club, there was no indication that Terry would not retire a Chelsea man.

The Blues’ skipper’s announcement in January 2016, then, came as a shock to the Chelsea faithful, bringing notice to the seemingly premature — even if inevitable — fall of the curtain on a legendary career.

After making his debut in the League Cup against Aston Villa late in 1998, John Terry made sporadic appearances under Gianluca Vialli, before joining Nottingham Forest on a short loan spell. He broke into the first team in 2000-01, when manager Claudio Ranieri handed him 22 Premier League appearances during a season that the 20-year-old would finish as the club’s Player of the Year.

It would be the first of several achievements to come.

Terry’s importance to the team grew as Ranieri relied on his partnership with then-captain Marcel Desailly to mastermind Chelsea’s progression from a fashionable mid-table club to a Champions League team that meant business. They received a major shot in the arm when Russian billionaire Roman Abramovich bought the club in 2003. It was also a significant year in Terry’s international career as he made his England debut against Serbia and Montenegro in June.

The season that followed saw Chelsea finish above perennial winners Manchester United for the first time in Premier League history, and defeat Premiership invincibles Arsenal en route to the club’s first Champions League semifinal. Terry ended the season making a first of four appearances in the PFA Team of the Year, and went to Portugal for the European Championships having displaced Sol Campbell as England’s first choice centre-back.

In the summer of 2004, Chelsea brought in Jose Mourinho, who was fresh from winning a treble with the unfancied FC Porto and raring to take on bigger challenges. The 23-year-old Terry was named captain as Chelsea embarked on the most successful period in the club’s history. In the three seasons that followed, Chelsea won 2 league cups, 2 Premier League titles and the FA Cup — success built on a core of John Terry, Frank Lampard, Petr Cech and Didier Drogba, Chelsea’s ‘old guard’.

This was also a period when Terry picked up several individual accolades. He was named PFA Player of the Year in 2005, the first defender to win the award since Paul McGrath in 1993. He would make a first of five consecutive appearances in the FIFPro World XI in 2005, as well as a first of four appearances in the UEFA Team of the Year.

He was also voted Chelsea’s Player of the Year for the second time in his career in 2006. Steve McClaren, hired as England manager after an underwhelming 2006 World Cup, named the Chelsea skipper as England captain.

Terry was now, beyond argument, one of football’s best.

However, more testing times were to come.

September 2007 saw the departure of Mourinho after a falling out with the club board. The season itself promised much but left a Chelsea squad dejected on three occasions as they saw the League Cup, the Premier League and the Champions League trophies go elsewhere.

For the European Cup in particular, Terry was left with no one but himself to blame as he slipped for the crucial penalty, a moment he has said will haunt him forever. Chelsea and Terry experienced further European heartbreak the following season as Tom Henning Ovrebo had a refereeing performance to forget at Stamford Bridge, handing Barcelona a berth in the final and eventually the trophy.

In early 2010, when he was revealed as the English footballer who had an affair with Vanessa Perroncel, Wayne Bridge’s ex-girlfriend — a horrendous personal error that cost him his status as England captain — it made him the perennial recipient of passionate booing across English grounds. After the revelation, Chelsea travelled to Burnley. Amidst a frosty reception, he scored a late winner to put Carlo Ancelotti’s side back on track in the title race, one they would go on to win in some style. All of this typified John Terry — imperfect, but unshakeable.

Terry had built an unflappable reputation as a top class defender, leader and hard man. He said about himself, “I still say if the ball is there to be won I will go for it, whether with my head or whatever, and if it means us scoring or stopping a goal, I won’t think twice.”

The period that followed, however, was not good for Chelsea or their captain. The team finished the 2010-11 season trophyless, and Carlo Ancelotti paid for it with his job. This was the first of two times in Terry’s career where he and his club would have an extremely underwhelming season following a dominant one, and it also marked the first attempt to phase him out of the first team.

New manager Andre Villas-Boas attempted to introduce a high defensive line that left Terry exposed on a number of occasions, and saw the young Portuguese manager fall back on quicker defenders to implement his system. He was also determined to make lesser use of Frank Lampard and displace Didier Drogba with Fernando Torres. These were unpopular moves that led to poor results and eventually his sacking. Terry was not helped by another personal abberation, mouthing racial profanity at Anton Ferdinand of QPR, an act that saw him land a lengthy ban and damage his position in the England squad almost beyond repair.

Interim manager Roberto Di Matteo reinstated the old guard, and was rewarded with the ultimate prize — the first Champions League in Chelsea’s history.

Terry retired from international football following EURO 2012, leaving him to focus on his club career. However, further rotation was to follow during the reign of Rafael Benitez, who played Terry only in games of lesser importance. This was something he could do with relative impunity owing to the fact that his stock could not have fallen any further among Chelsea fans.

The writing was seemingly on the wall, however. Unsavoury incidents were fresher in the memory than individual accolades, the skipper was out of favour for two seasons running, and was well over 30 years of age. Was John Terry done?

Mourinho did not share the views of Benitez and Villas-Boas. Where they saw a slowing, easily-exposed has-been, he saw an experienced warrior with an excellent reading of the game who could form a title-winning partnership with the quicker Gary Cahill.

Terry grabbed the opportunity he was handed with gusto, performing with excellence in Mourinho’s lower defensive block. The English pair formed the core of a defence that would go on to win the club’s fourth Premier League title in 2015, leading the table from the opening day to the end. It was a landmark achievement for Terry in particular as he played every minute of a league campaign for the first time in his career, aged 34.

Once again they tried to put him down. Once again he fed off it and rose tall.

Chelsea did not start the defence of their title well at all, gathering just 4 points from the first 4 matches. Mourinho, who asked Terry to take the club on his shoulders in 2004 and stood by him for two seasons in his second stint, hauled off his skipper at half-time at the Etihad in the second game of the season, and began to rotate him out of the team, giving an increasing number of starts to the young Kurt Zouma.

The season did not take much of a turn for the better even under interim manager Guus Hiddink, particularly in a defensive sense as the Blues continued to let in goals during a meek climb to the top half of the table, with or without Terry in the side.

A sending off at the Stadium of Light following an injury layoff is not the kind of ending that the fans desired for their beloved captain, who has emerged from the dugout 703 times in Chelsea colours and has been the face of the club through the most successful period in their history.

Offered a new deal by the club last week, the skipper responded, “The contract extension the club has offered me is a different role and I hope everyone will understand I want to take the time to consider it carefully before making a decision.” While fans will hope — for reasons emotional as well as those to do with football — that Terry stays on, the chances look slim.

Should the captain leave the ship, the Blues supporters’ emotions are best summed up by a certain banner that embellishes the Shed End: Captain, Leader, Legend.
