#1766. Tuchel learns lesson as England clinch third place in 10-goal thriller

Was this evidence of England head coach Thomas Tuchel already learning lessons from the Argentina collapse? Let’s hope so.

With England on the ropes and in danger of throwing away a lead against France, Tuchel resisted the temptation to flood his team with defenders and was rewarded with a World Cup bronze medal.

England looked on course to secure an emphatic victory to clinch the nation’s best World Cup finish since 1966 and yet Tuchel was left with the exact same scenario that had gone so badly against Argentina in the semi-final.

Leading by four goals at half-time, England somehow went into the final hydration break of this bronze medal game with a single-goal advantage. This time, Tuchel steered England over the line by getting his late substitutions right.

Jude Bellingham stepped off the bench to cap a wonderful tournament for him with the goal that made sure England finished the World Cup in third place.

It may have resembled an exhibition match at times, with France failing to turn up in the first half. But England’s thrilling 6-4 victory will send Tuchel home from the United States feeling a little bit better, even though he is not yet off the hook for what happened in Atlanta.

The fact that success against France was earned with a Bukayo Saka hat-trick, as well as goals from Declan Rice, Ezri Konsa and Bellingham, will prompt more debate over Tuchel’s decision-making when it really mattered. Not least why Saka watched the entire Argentina game from the substitutes’ bench.

Tuchel cut a relaxed figure, changing his touchline attire to a casual white T-shirt and tracksuit bottoms. But his team meant business, as they raced into a stunning four-goal first-half lead.

Saka played like a man with a point to prove. He scored twice and produced the shot from which England won the corner for Konsa’s goal in the opening 45 minutes. Was this a message to Tuchel or simply the winger taking out his frustration on France?

France looked uninterested from the start and it was a loose Désiré Doué pass that gifted possession to Rice. As England’s captain for the evening strode forwards, Doué did not bother to track him and Rice curled a lovely shot into the corner of the net to give Tuchel’s team a third-minute lead.

It's a quick start from England! 🦁⚡Declan Rice fires home the opener in the third minute against France ⚽ pic.twitter.com/ID4u3rXOuM

Having been criticised for sending on three defenders against Argentina, Tuchel started with five attacking players on the pitch and just Rice in front of the defence.

Saka had a goal correctly ruled out for offside before his shot was blocked for a corner, from which England doubled their lead. Rice turned provider, as he sent in a perfect delivery that was headed past goalkeeper Mike Maignan by Konsa five minutes before the first hydration break.

The Three Lions double their lead! 🦁⚽Ezri Konsa rises highest from Declan Rice's corner to head home 🙌 pic.twitter.com/8BfI1LSDOQ

While Tuchel would have been delighted with his team’s start to the game, Saka’s influence raises just as many questions as answers.

Saka was the next England player on the scoresheet. He sent Marcus Rashford away on goal. Rashford’s shot was saved, but England kept the ball alive and Saka eventually found the back of the net via a deflection.

The Three Lions lead France by three goals! 🦁🔥Bukayo Saka finishing off a quick England counter-attack ⚽ pic.twitter.com/9SCfE3uH3v

England had been given much sterner tests by DR Congo and Panama, and yet Tuchel’s players deserve praise for capitalising on such a terrible first-half performance from France.

Ebererchi Eze could not have believed that he was given the time and space to turn and pick out Saka on the stroke of half-time. He did so superbly and Saka easily added England’s fourth goal.

🗣 "France are being taken apart by England!" Bukayo Saka scores his second for the Three Lions' FOURTH goal against the two-time world champions 🤯 pic.twitter.com/4RshXY692E

It perhaps summed up France’s mentality that Kylian Mbappé, who threatened on a couple of occasions in the first half, reacted to England’s fourth goal with what appeared to be a slight smirk.

Tuchel’s name had been booed by some of those, mostly neutral supporters, inside the Hard Rock Stadium ahead of kick-off.

His star has undoubtedly fallen as a result of the Argentina defeat and yet nobody could have failed to have been impressed by what his and his players produced in the first half on Saturday night, however bad France had been.

When Tuchel made a change at half-time, there was no Dan Burn sent on to try to see out a 4-0 win. Instead, it was an attacking substitution with Ollie Watkins replacing Rashford. It immediately backfired, but Tuchel was later rewarded for trying to remain positive.

Watkins’s first act was to lose the ball on the halfway line to start a France attack that ended in a goal. Michael Olise played in Mbappé, who slotted the ball past Dean Henderson, who was given a rare chance ahead of Jordan Pickford.

France substitute Bradley Barcola pulled another goal back in the 54th minute, which meant that England’s four-goal advantage had been halved in just nine second-half minutes.

There was still no call for Burn, as Tuchel stuck to his gung-ho approach and Henderson had to save well from Ousmane Dembélé, who had also been sent on at the break. England had lost their balance with the half-time change and Olise was the next France attacker to go close.

Dembélé tested Henderson again before Mbappé got France’s third goal just before the final hydration break to pass Lionel Messi as the World Cup’s all-time top scorer. Like they had against Argentina, England had dropped deep and invited pressure as their opposition grew in confidence.

Kylian Mbappe scores his 22nd World Cup goal to become the leading goalscorer in the history of the competition ⚽🔥👏 pic.twitter.com/sDTNnW0kLZ

Having led so comfortably at half-time, England went into the final quarter of the game with a slender one-goal lead – just as they had against Argentina in Atlanta.

Olise somehow missed a sitter after arriving late on the end of a low ball across the penalty area and Tuchel decided it was time for more changes. But it was Elliot Anderson and Bellingham he called for, rather than any extra defenders, and it ultimately paid dividends.

Bellingham almost dribbled his way through to put the result beyond doubt, before Olise squandered another wonderful opportunity. Mercifully, Djed Spence won an 85th-minute penalty that allowed Saka to complete his hat-trick.

Bukayo Saka completes his hat-trick from the penalty spot! ⚽3️⃣England lead France 5-3 in the closing stages of this game 🦁 pic.twitter.com/EnYOg8UAvT

There was still time for Dembélé to briefly up England’s anxiety levels again, before Bellingham put the finishing touch to what has been an outstanding World Cup for him with a brilliant goal.

Jude Bellingham grabbing England's SIXTH goal against France! 🦁Driving over the halfway line before firing a shot into the bottom corner 🔥👏 pic.twitter.com/l0B0BVs548

The players made sure to invite Jason Steele on to the stage to receive a medal. The Brighton goalkeeper is not in England’s World Cup squad, but travelled to North America as a training goalkeeper.

Of course I would love to have played more but it’s too late to talk about that. I try to do my talking on the pitch and it’s done now, move on. I’m fit.

We built and built across the tournament. We had some amazing results and in the end we fell short against Argentina. It hurts a lot to all of us and I’m sure it’s the same to the fans back home but we have to hold out head high and focus on the next one.

France are not hanging around for the ceremony. They are down the tunnel as organisers set up a stage to hand out the bronze medals. Probably sums up their attitude to the game.

Enough for four matches, what happened here. We had a brilliant first half, then a turbulent second half. You could see the difference of what one day makes and the difference in the schedule. We are so, so tired and drained from the last weeks.

So a massive compliment and full respect - the mentality that we showed. Going through all the adversity is absolutely brilliant.

I was afraid of the physical demands of the match. We know the quality and speed of France, and they have much less schedule for them. It was less demanding.

They had one more day in-between the semi-final to digest, and they had way less travel distances than us.

We played in the heat, at altitude. I was worried physically. You could see it in the second half, the cramps and all the tiredness, but I was never worried about the mentality.

I have said it before, this team has created something very special, and they showed it again.

However we got here England have had their best World Cup since 1966. Whatever criticism Thomas Tuchel received after Argentina defeat he deserves to keep his job and the chance to put things right in 2028 #england

Some players from France and England are huddled near the halfway line praying. Among them are Dayot Upamecano, Maxence Lacroix, Trevoh Chalobah and Bukayo Saka. Very different atmosphere to the Argentina defeat three days ago in Atlanta. They are playing Wonderwall here as they prepare for the bronze medals to be handed out but it is not very celebratory this time.

When does the second set start? That was as much as you could hope for from a third/fourth-place play-off. Some slack defending, some high-quality combination play and lots of entertainment. England’s victory stops things spiralling further for Tuchel, but there will be a sense of what might have been, not least the fact Saka played no part in the semi-final.

Bellingham’s seventh goal of the tournament, which is the highest tally by an England player at a World Cup. The game was stretched, but it was a fantastic individual goal from Bellingham, carrying the ball forward from the halfway line. He showed great composure not to take the shot too early, taking extra touches to finish with aplomb.

A seventh goal of the tournament for Jude Bellingham! 7️⃣⭐The most EVER by an Englishman at a single World Cup 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿👏 pic.twitter.com/YACnNWvqW1

Good work from Reece James to keep the ball and then defend well against Barcola.

What a barmy game this has been. Upamecano started the move with good defending and a surge forward, and then Dembele cuts inside Chalobah and buries a shot into the bottom corner.

🇫🇷 Ousmane Dembele scores France's fourth goal against England ⚽ pic.twitter.com/U4gCVb1tQw

Spence down and receiving some treatment for cramp after winning a challenge against Olise. France not happy with the stoppage in the game.

Excellent Rice challenge, and then Bellingham wins a free-kick in midfield. Rice can hardly run yet managed to time his challenge well. Trevoh Chalobah replaces Marc Guehi.

Seven minutes of added time to play, and France have just been caught offside from their own short corner.

That is England’s first World Cup hat-trick since Harry Kane scored three against Panama in the 2018 finals. But Bukayo Saka’s treble is also the last England hat-trick in all competitions since.... Bukayo Saka. The Arsenal forward also scored three times in the win over North Macedonia in 2023.

That was very unselfish from Jude Bellingham, because had he scored the penalty it would have been his seventh goal of the tournament. That would be the most goals scored by an England player at a World Cup.

Sends Maignan the wrong way, and picks out the bottom corner. Saka has his hat-trick, and England are surely assured of third place and the bronze medal/trophy. England’s players will be most pleased to avoid extra time.

Bukayo Saka completes his hat-trick from the penalty spot! ⚽3️⃣England lead France 5-3 in the closing stages of this game 🦁 pic.twitter.com/EnYOg8UAvT

Won by Djed Spence, who was too sharp by Malo Gusto. Once the England full-back got his toe to the ball, it was a stonewall penalty. Morgan Rogers played the pass to release him on the overlap.

Bellingham or Saka for the hat-trick? Bellingham has the ball in his hands, but then passes it to Saka for the hat-trick.

Qunsah off, Reece James on. That also looks a case of cramp in very humid conditions in Miami.

Now Olise misses a sitter! Great interplay in the box involving Olise and Dembele, five-a-side football between the France forwards, but the finish was lacking. Olise, and then the referee, receive some treatment for cramp.

England with a great chance to wrap the game up but Bellingham fluffed his lines! Burst through, the benefit of fresh legs, but he carried the ball too close to Maignan and then Rogers’s follow up was blocked.

Ivan Toney and Eberechi Eze are the players coming off, Bellingham and Anderson on, which adds some strength to England’s midfield.

That is a big cheer for Bellingham coming on, one of the stars of the World Cup and appreciated by the neutral. His job here is to see out a win.

France continue to dominate, and they have a free-kick in a crossing position. Cleared by Eze. Elliott Anderson is ready to come on, as well as Bellingham. Digne finds Mbappe, but Konsa makes a good block. Rogers then does well to make it stick and buy a foul.

Great chance for France to equalise, but Michael Olise opened up his foot too much and his shot flew past the post. France look like scoring every time they venture into England’s defensive third. Mbappe goes down looking for a penalty, but nothing doing, before Digne fouls Saka in the box. May have been knee on knee contact, looked a sore one for Saka. Bellingham is ready to come on.

Rice is still out there, soldiering on. Somewhat surprising that Tuchel has not added fresh legs since his half-time changes. Better spell of possession in the last few minutes from England. There have been 15 shots on target in this game.

Play has stopped immediately after the goal for the hydration break. Tuchel mist be thinking about changes. Rice is struggling.

A penny for Mikel Arteta's thoughts watching this: if one of his first comments during pre-season isn't an eruption about how Declan Rice has been asked to play again, he will have mellowed. He's as tired as an also ran at the end of the Grand National.

This is a fantastic France goal, razor sharp link up play between Mbappe and Olise at the edge of the box, and the France captain’s finish was unerring. Drilled into the bottom corner with his left foot. Liquid football. Defending remains optional in this game, but that goal would have graced any game. Mbappe’s 22nd World Cup goal.

Over to you Lionel! Mbappe’s 10th goal of the World Cup means he is the clear leader in the Golden Boot table - but Lionel Messi has a chance in the final tomorrow to add to his eight goals. You would not bet against Mbappe adding to his total here. England have been guilty of dropping deep again, just like they did against Argentina. They are a 4-4-2 with Ollie Watkins and Ivan Toney partnering each other. This was just before the “hydration”, so Tuchel could change it up now.

Kylian Mbappe scores his 22nd World Cup goal to become the leading goalscorer in the history of the competition ⚽🔥👏 pic.twitter.com/sDTNnW0kLZ

There is a loud chant coming from the stands: “Mexico!” That shows the diversity of the crowd here, with empty seats in sections including the England supporters. In just one small block of fans in front of the press box, there are shirts from Colombia, Inter Miami, Chile and USA.

France should probably be back to within one goal, but Ousmane Dembele scuffed his shot from a favourable position in the box and it was a simple save for Henderson. Then the goalkeeper pushes away a long-range hit by Upamecano.

Delightful scooped pass over the top of the France defence by Eze but Toney could not bring the ball under his spell off his chest. Then Spence does brilliantly to win a tackle and then turn defence into attakc with a surging run forward.

Morgan Rogers with a sloppy pass inside his own half, and Olise fires wide from the edge of the box. He had so much time and space to line it up. Some fatigue starting to show in England’s legs now.

This is what Tuchel was talking about when he discussed England playing under pressure. France have decided to show up and all of a sudden the deficit is only two goals. Get ready for a testing half an hour.

England go close to another set-piece goal, but Maignan saves well after Toney rose to meet Rice’s inswinging delivery. There are surely going to be more goals in this game.

Henderson stands up well to save from Dembele, but the flag belatedly was raised for offside. A lot of wasted energy for Declan Rice, who had sprinted back some 60 yards to defend. England now the team being repeatedly exposed in transition.

Mbappe with the ball inside Quansah, who loses track of Barcola and with his pace that is always fatal. It looked like Barcola might have overrun the ball, but he got his shot off in time to find the bottom corner.

It's a second goal for France! 🇫🇷Kylian Mbappe's long pass finds Bradley Barcola who fires home 🔥 pic.twitter.com/h4GvkBZOSN

Great play from Eze, close control and quick feet to skip through two or three France challenges in midfield, and he tried to chip Maignan from the halfway line. Always drifting wide.

Composed football from England, playing out from deep in their own half with Rice finding Rogers between the lines. Saka with a pass into Watkins but his shot was tame. Then England and Spence were caught forward, but Rice got his toe to the ball ahead of Olise. Then Rabiot volleys not far wide. Chances galore in this game.

France reduce the deficit through Mbappe’s ninth goal of the tournament. Watkins was caught in possession by Upamecano on halfway, and France found Olise free in the No 10 zone. Lovely through ball splits the England defence, and Mbappe finishes first time beyond Henderson with his left foot.

France hit back after the break! 🇫🇷💥Kylian Mbappe pulls one back with his ninth goal at the 2026 World Cup ⚽ pic.twitter.com/Hxfg1s46ER

Hernandez, Konate, Cherki and Doue off, Digne, Upamecano, Barcola and Dembele on for France.

Ollie Watkins replaces Marcus Rashford for England.

England will fly back home tonight with the feel-good factor of a win against a World Cup heavyweight but it would be foolish to think any of Thomas Tuchel’s problems are solved. In fact, Bukayo Saka’s two first-half goals only leads to the question: why was he left on the bench against Argentina? And Ezri Konsa for that matter. England did not lose a game that Konsa started and it was harsh to bench him against Argentina last Wednesday.

No frustration, I’m a little bit emotional, I can’t find the words to describe just how proud I am of these players. They are playing a game with broken hearts, I see 11 lads out there with broken hearts. I’ve seen them around the hotel the last few days, broken hearts. They can build a performance like that just through pride of playing for England, the team spirit we’ve built over the last seven weeks it’s been a privilege to watch. I know the cynics will say it is too late but we still play against a world class opponent.

4 - France have conceded four first half goals for the first time since a EURO qualification match against Yugoslavia in April 1968.WOW. pic.twitter.com/SePSwONNA8

Well, hands up who had this scoreline on their “bronze final” bingo card? A scarcely believable 45 minutes, and England have surely secured third place for this World Cup. There has been a lot to like about their attacking play, but for many it will make the frustration of Argentina sting all the more. France have been half-hearted in their defensive approach, but England have put them to the sword in style.

Just the four minutes of first-half stoppage time to play.

It is not a consequential game, but this is still a heck of a half from England. They are making mincemeat of a ragged France team. Eze with a lovely turn in midfield and through ball to his Arsenal team-mate Saka, and he found the bottom corner with an early finish. Four goals before half time.

🗣 "France are being taken apart by England!" Bukayo Saka scores his second for the Three Lions' FOURTH goal against the two-time world champions 🤯 pic.twitter.com/4RshXY692E

France are playing like they have been on the beach since their semi-final defeat by Spain last Tuesday. Tuchel won’t read too much into England’s best finish at a World Cup since 1966. He wants his team to perform under pressure and there has been none of that in this game.

Almost a fourth for England, Rashford’s low cross seemed to run under Toney’s foot when the striker would have had a tap in. Moments earlier, there was another great defensive recovery from Rice to block a Gusto pass.

Saka with a curling cross which is just beyond Rogers and drifts wide of the far post. France showing no signs of tightening up.

Breaking in behind this France high line has been like shelling peas for England. Saka’s pass initially released Rashford on the break, and he had plenty of time to think when running through on goal. Maignan saved, Saka’s rebound was blocked, but it feel back for Rashford who kept his head and picked out Saka who passed the ball into an unguarded net. Pretty farcical France defending.

That was a very close offside call from VAR for Saka’s goal. With Mike Maignan out of his goal, England needed to stay behind two France defenders. Marcus Rashford was about a foot onside before teeing up the third.

The Three Lions lead France by three goals! 🦁🔥Bukayo Saka finishing off a quick England counter-attack ⚽ pic.twitter.com/9SCfE3uH3v

Good save from Dean Henderson to deny Mbappe, who sat down two England defenders. You were waiting for the net to ripple, but his effort was too close to Henderson.

Then England break and Saka is in behind the France back four again, but his first touch is a little heavy, and he can neither get his shot off nor round Maignan.

England looking lively in attack again, Rashford with a delicious nutmeg on Zaire-Emery, before unleashing a swerving shot from almost 30 yards. Maignan was scrambling but he made the save. Rice then makes another ball recovery in midfield.

There is a bronze medal at stake but this match has the feel of an exhibition. There is no intensity to France’s press. Michael Olise is extremely hard-working usually but has allowed opponents to run past him. Players are only coming alive with the ball at their feet.

Quick feet from Mbappe inside the England box, but Declan Rice was well-positioned to win an important challenge. Half an hour into the game, and Mbappe is yet to nudge ahead of Messi in the Golden Boot race.

Guehi with a goal-line clearance after Mbappe squeezed a shot beyond Henderson, but the flag was up for offside in any case. It looked a close call on the replays, was a clever pass by Doue to find Mbappe. Henderson also did well to get something on the shot.

Play has now resumed, and England are back on the front foot after a Rice diagonal out to Quansah.

Time for the first hydration break of the game. Miami is one of the World Cup venues where it is probably appreciated.

You can only play the game in front of you, but England have done that well so far. They find Toney free in the box, but he cannot get his shot off on the swivel.

Mbappe laughing as we walks back to the halfway line, so France are not feeling too stressed, but England are 2-0 up in Miami. Good inswinging delivery from Rice, and Konsa rose highest on the six-yard line to glance a header into the far corner.

The Three Lions double their lead! 🦁⚽Ezri Konsa rises highest from Declan Rice's corner to head home 🙌 pic.twitter.com/8BfI1LSDOQ

Saka is causing France’s defence all manner of problems, this time Eze released him in behind the French defence. Lacroix did well to stick to his task and deflect Saka’s shot over the bar for a corner.

Marc Guehi sticks out a leg to block Mbappe’s low cross after the French forward dropped a shoulder and showed his burst of speed over a few yards. England defend the corner. The game continues to feel open, there’s more space for the attackers on the pitch than there would be in a semi-final.

Bukayo Saka has the ball in the net but the flag goes up for offside. Correct decision, he had just strayed a yard ahead of Hernandez. It was a crisp finish, cutting back inside and finding the bottom corner with his left foot. England finding it quite easy to get in behind France.

The entertainment continues: Cherki with a strike from the edge of the D, which was parried by Henderson before Spence hurried his clearance. Zaire-Emery picked up the loose ball but could not do enough with it.

He did not know too much about it, but an important recovery run from Spence enables him to get his heel to the ball when it looked like Mbappe was away. England continue to move the ball well, looking quite fluent going forward, which will only serve to frustrate fans further.

England flowing forward again, Saka in behind Hernandez and lifting in a cross that came all the way to Rashford at the far post. One touch to control, the second to shoot, but his effort was blocked, deflected behind for a corner. Rice’s delivery is too deep.

Mbappe with a shot inside the England box but it is blocked by the legs of Rice. This kind of game tends to be either soporific or care-free and entertaining, and it feels like this is going to be the latter.

That was Declan Rice’s first World Cup goal – and a beauty of a strike at that. It is still a strange decision to play him and add to his workload. This is not a game to judge Thomas Tuchel’s team on either, as France are not playing with urgency.

Doue with a sloppy pass across midfield when there was a chance for France to break, and Declan Rice intercepted. No France defender stepped out to engage the Arsenal man, and he was able to carry the ball forward unopposed. The finish was sweet, the ball was passed into the bottom corner from just outside the box.

It's a quick start from England! 🦁⚡Declan Rice fires home the opener in the third minute against France ⚽ pic.twitter.com/ID4u3rXOuM

The early indications are that Eze is playing in a deeper midfield position alongside Rice. Good pass from Dean Henderson into the free man Djed Spece behind France’s press. Then Rashford whips in a promising cross form the left towards Ivan Toney.

As expected, there are a fair few empty seats here. In the end where some England fans seem to be congregated there are blocks of green seats visible from the opposite end of the stadium. It could be quite a strange atmosphere with most of the supporters inside the stadium neutrals. There are a lot of Mexico and Colombia shirts.

For the penultimate time in this tournament, it’s time for the giant flags on the pitch and the anthems. Rice and Mbappe lead out their teams.

Tuchel booed when his name read out and picture shown at the Miami Stadium

This is a big evening for Dean Henderson making his first World Cup appearance. The Crystal Palace goalkeeper, 29, earns his sixth cap and an opportunity to stake his claim for the No1 jersey next season.

No, never [did he hesitate about playing them] because Declan gets more and more fit. He gets his fitness back and his health back and for Bukayo there’s no concerns. He didn’t start, he didn’t play in the semi-finals. He’s a key player for us and ready to go.

It’s just common sense. We have so many kilometres in the legs. We have so many travel kilometres in our bones. We have a day less recovery. We come from 10 men in altitude. We come from overtime here in Miami. These two guys, they gave everything physically in every match,. They were ready to go again but we keep them and have them to finish the match for us.

0 - This is England's first FIFA World Cup campaign to not see a Manchester United player feature in any of their games since 1958.Unused. pic.twitter.com/LN3L3e7q5q

We have to regroup, and we have to pick ourselves up and try to finish the tournament on a high.

I have always been hungry for this opportunity. It was frustrating. I only got a few minutes, but that is how football goes sometimes.

Now is my chance to prove I should have got more minutes. There’s a lot of goals in the team and on the bench.

Hopefully, we can bring goals, and hopefully we can finish the tournament on a win.

Thomas Tuchel has risked angering Arsenal by selecting Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka for this game. Rice has been recovering from illness and was running on empty for the last two games. He has also suffered neural pain in his hamstring and describes himself as playing “an obscene amount of games”. This is surely a chance to have a breather. Saka has been managing an Achilles injury all tournament and did not feature against Argentina on Wednesday.

2 - Declan Rice is the second Arsenal player to start a major tournament game for England as captain (World Cup/EURO) after Tony Adams at EURO 1996.Privilege. pic.twitter.com/MWlX7HiWXX

Seven changes to the team that was beaten by Spain, with Zaire-Emery starting in midfield. Rayan Cherki is preferred to Ousmane Dembele.

France XI: Maignan; T. Hernández, Lacroix, Konate, Gusto; Rabiot, Zaïre-Emery; Doue, Cherki, Olise, Mbappe

Subs: Akliouche, Barcola, Dembele, Digne, L. Hernandez, Kante, Kone, Kounde, Mateta, Risser, Saliba, Samba, Tchouameni, Thuram, Upamecano

Some of Tuchel’s regular starters do drop to the bench: Pickford, Kane and Bellingham the notable names. Slightly surprising that Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka both start given their ongoing niggles. It is a very attacking team with Rice sitting behind Morgan Rogers and Eze. Is Tuchel making a point there?

England XI: D. Henderson; Quansah, Konsa, Guehi, Spence; Rice, Eze; Saka, Rogers, Rashford; Toney

Subs: Pickford, O’Reilly, Stones, Anderson, Kane, Bellingham, Chalobah, J. Henderson, Burn, Gordon, Watkins, Madueke, Trafford, James

Kobbie Mainoo’s back injury means that he not only misses out today, but it also means he ends this World Cup without playing a single minute of the tournament. Ivan Toney gets his first start and you’d imagine Trevoh Chalobah will get off the substitutes’ bench at some stage for his first World Cup minutes. It’s certainly an attacking team, but it’s also a slightly strange one.

Our XI to face France 💪 pic.twitter.com/UexpADmHPr

Matt Law was one of the journalists in Tuchel’s absorbing pre-match press conference, and says he appeared wounded and possibly shaken. Matt writes: “There was some spikiness from Tuchel, when he deflected the odd question back to the reporter who asked it, and he was fidgety when not speaking, messing with the earpiece in front of him on the desk and twisting the wires. He did not look comfortable.”

The Morgan Rogers transfer to Chelsea means that two England players have moved for a British record fee during this World Cup.

Elliot Anderson moved to Manchester City for £116m and Rogers has cost Chelsea £117m. That means England have two players who have moved for a combined £233m during this tournament.

England vice-captain Declan Rice cost Arsenal more than £100m in 2023. I haven’t done the maths, but it’s fair to guess that England’s first-choice starting line up would be worth near enough £1bn.

He takes an excellent set-piece and his athleticism is to be admired, but do you ever see him dictate the tempo of a match in the way that Rodri will attempt to do for Spain when they face Argentina on Sunday in New Jersey? The blunt answer is no. He doesn’t have cute, clever balls in his armoury.

There was a bolt of lightning in the distance on arrival at the Hard Rock Stadium. The last thing this Bronze match needs is a delay to prolong the agony of this match. John Stones was distraught doing his pre-match media duties yesterday. It is harsh to ask players to get themselves up for this game after the devastation of losing to Argentina on Wednesday.

Morgan Rogers is on his way to Chelsea for a record £117m fee, in news which comes as a blow to Arsenal’s summer transfer plans. Rogers started the semi-final on England’s right flank and he is likely to be involved again tonight.

He leaves France having won a World Cup and reached the final in another. This team has arguably played the best football of the lot, but will finish empty-handed. The smart money is on Zinedine Zidane replacing him, who won three consecutive Champions Leagues while Real Madrid head coach. So he knows his way around knockout football.

Neither England nor France wanted to be playing this game in Miami, but they can have no complaints about the nature of their semi-final defeats.

Tournament favourites France were comprehensively outplayed by Spain, with their feted front four of Kylian Mbappe, Ousmane Dembele, Bradley Barcola and Michael Olise all turning in below-par performances.

England’s defeat by Argentina was perhaps not as much of a surprise, but the nature of Thomas Tuchel’s team’s second-half collapse was just as alarming as France’s no-show.

England’s manager was fiercely criticised for replacing Anthony Gordon with Ezri Konsa and switching to a back five in the 72nd minute, but Tuchel has since defended his decisions.

“If you are asking if I regret my decisions, if this is the question, then I say no. I don’t regret my ‌decisions because I ‌felt that we became ⁠too passive,” said Tuchel.

“I took several decisions, trusting my instinct, my intuition, my experience, trusting my competitiveness, and I took the decision in order to help the team and get the result.

“I would regret if I didn’t help. I would regret ⁠if we didn’t react, but I have no regrets over the decision itself.”

Quite how strong Didier Deschamps and Tuchel decide to go with their teams is anyone’s guess. There has been some suggestion that Mbappe will start to give him the chance to beat Lionel Messi to the Golden Boot.

Some of England’s regular starters, such as Declan Rice, look physically spent, so there could be some rotation, and even a chance for players such as Kobbie Mainoo who has not played a minute of football at the tournament.

The third/fourth-place play-off has been rebranded as the “Bronze Final” for this tournament, and Tuchel was keen to point out that finishing third would be England’s best World Cup result since 1966. They lost this fixture against Belgium in 2018, but the way that game has been widely forgotten speaks volumes.

Arsenal and Saliba decided not to go down the surgical route and instead favoured a conservative treatment programme, but there were fears that the centre-back may have missed the remainder of 2027.

#1763. A chip off the old block? Wayne Rooney's son Kai, 16, is dazzling in Man United's academy after scoring FOUR goals in a game - insiders reveal the secrets behind his rise

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 07:00 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 07:06 EDT, 1 November 2026

Just over 24 years ago, a 16-year-old footballing phenomenon called Wayne Rooney made his mark with that goal for Everton against Arsenal.

Fast-forward to now and his eldest son, Kai, enhanced his burgeoning reputation while in action for Manchester United's Under 18s on Tuesday.

The 16-year-old, who turns 17 on Monday, scored four goals for the young Red Devils in a 6-0 thrashing of Burnley's U18s in the Under-18 Premier League North.

His four goals showed his repertoire of skills as the forward scored two with his preferred left foot, one with his head and the other a fine run that was finished with his right foot.

His four goals came in 44 minutes across half-time - with the latter three coming in a devastating 15-minute second-half spell (49, 63 and 66 minutes).

As Manchester United's own match report on their website details the teenager 'was the star of a clinical showing after the break from Darren Fletcher's side'.

Kai Rooney opens the scoring at Burnley for our #MUAcademy U18s 💪Watch live coverage on MUTV ⤵️ pic.twitter.com/KFr8B2hWNY

Kai Rooney scored four goals for Manchester United U18s as they thrashed Burnley U18s 6-0

One of his goals came was a penalty during Tuesday's Under-18 Premier League North fixture

Rooney's father Wayne scored that goal against Arsenal as a 16-year-old for Everton in 2002

Rooney then followed that performance with another goal in Saturday's comeback 4-1 win at Blackburn Rovers U18s, although he was later sent off for two bookable offences.

Just like his dad Wayne, Kai is fixated on football and is following in his father's footsteps in a number of ways.

As detailed by Daily Mail Sport in January, one of those is with regards to diet.

Akin to his famous father - who is United's all-time record goalscorer - in his Old Trafford heyday, Rooney Jr eats plenty of carbohydrates two days before a game. This then changes to salmon and rice followed by rice pudding the night before matches.

His dietary discipline has been recognised by those within the United academy - who are impressed by Rooney's focus.

The teenager does allow himself some respite at times though with the family's go-to is Chinese takeaway 'WowYauChow' in Altrincham. As revealed in Manchester United Confidential, crispy chilli beef is a particular favourite of the rising footballer.

Cooking has also become a passion for Rooney off-the-pitch and he is also fluent in Spanish - a trait that will only stand him in good stead in the multicultural world of football.

Rooney has had to deal with accusations of nepotism, due to the legendary figure of who his dad is, but he has always wanted to form his own path - even from a younger age than he is now.

'Kai told Wayne to stop coming to football games when he played grassroots tournaments and stuff, because he used to get swarmed, and he couldn't even watch the game,' his mum Coleen explained during her time in the I'm A Celebrity… Get Me Out Of Here! jungle almost two years ago.

Kai is pictured with parents Coleen and Wayne signing his Man United contract when younger

Rooney is fixated with football like his father but wants to forge his own career within the sport

'How do you say to all of these kids, "Go away, I'm watching my son?" Adults, it's different, you could speak to them, so he [Kai] just said, "Oh, dad, there's no point you coming because you don't even watch me play anyway". Which is sad, but it can't be helped.'

Speaking in August 2024, Rooney underlined that he is intent on doing things his own way.

'I'm trying to make a name for myself, not try and be my dad because I'm my own person,' Kai said back in August 2024.

'I want to see how my career goes, obviously try to do the best I can and try to reach the biggest stages.

'I'm just focusing on me and to try to not let any pressure get to me and just keep working on me day by day, month by month.'

Rooney Jr has copied his father's diet when he was a professional - which includes salmon

His parents, meanwhile, have been keen to stress that they are keeping the pressure off their young son.

'He has great coaches at Manchester United, so I take a stand-off approach,' Wayne told the BBC last year.

'I speak to him, but for me it’s all about his mentality and his mindset, to make sure he keeps enjoying it – that’s the main thing for me.'

Meanwhile Coleen told The Times earlier this year: 'He’s lived it (being Wayne's son) from a young age. When we used to go to matches when he was younger, he’d get a lot of people coming up saying, "Oh, are you Wayne Rooney’s son?"

'But he’s strong-minded, always has been. I’ve got no worries in the way he deals with it.'

A Puma ambassador since he was 12, Kai used to play football in laceless boots after previously breaking both of his feet.

The youngster was signed up by Puma at the age of 12 - and has pursued a football career

Against Burnley his boots had laces as he tied his opponents in knots, something he will look to continue to do as he makes his own way in the game.

And while replicating his father seems fanciful, the iconic 'remember the name' piece of commentary could be updated for Kai in the future.

#1762. Torreense vs Ararat-Armenia - prediction, team news, lineups

By Freddie Cotton | 03 Nov 2026 16:08

Torreense welcome Ararat-Armenia to the Estadio Dr. Magalhaes Pessoa on Thursday evening for round four of the 2026-27 UEFA Europa League campaign.

In their previous European outing, Azul-grenas suffered a thumping 4-1 loss away to Hungarian side Ferencvaros, while the Black and Whites were also convincingly beaten by AZ Alkmaar at the Vazgen Sargsyan Republican Stadium.

Making history as the first side from the Portuguese second tier to ever compete in the competition after beating Sporting CP 2-1 in last season’s Taca de Portugal final, Torreense will be content with how they have started their maiden European campaign.

Having followed up a monumental triumph over Norwegian outfit Lillestrom in their opening fixture by losing back-to-back matches against Sunderland and Ferencvaros, Azul-grenas sit a lowly 28th in the Europa League table, though they are only outside of the knockout phase places on goal difference.

However, Torreense will be extremely disappointed with their start to the latest Liga Portugal 2 campaign as after finishing third and narrowly missing out on promotion to the top tier last season, Joao Nuno’s men have won only two of their opening nine league games to sit 12th in the table with just a two point buffer to the drop zone.

If they are to bounce back from consecutive European defeats on Thursday evening, the key for Azul-grenas could well be to patch up their leaky defence as despite only five teams surrendering fewer goals than them in the league this season, the Portuguese outfit have already conceded seven in their three matches on the continent.

Much like their opposition, Ararat-Armenia are creating history in the Europa League this season as the first Armenian team to ever participate in the main competition, but to the contrast of Torreense, the visitors have not had the start that they would have desired.

Falling to defeat in each of their opening three fixtures, the Black and Whites are one of four sides alongside Marseille, Celtic and Viktoria Plzen that are yet to pick up a single point after three games, though with their inferior goal difference, the Armenian side are currently rooted to the foot of the League Phase table.

On the other hand, Manuel Tulipa will be relatively happy with his side’s progress in the league, as following their first title triumph for six years last season, Ararat-Armenia sit second in the Armenian Premier League table and only two points behind leaders FC Noah, having not lost any of their previous seven outings.

With no prior encounters against Portuguese opposition, the Black and Whites could make history with a victory on Thursday evening, although they will also need to tighten up defensively if they are to climb off the bottom of the table, having shipped 11 goals in Europe so far – two more than any other side in the competition.

French forward Adama Baradji is the host’s only confirmed absentee for Thursday’s clash as the 19-year-old continues to recover from an undisclosed issue that has ruled him out for the last month.

Following back-to-back clean sheets, it is likely that Nuno deploys an identical defence to the one that started against Portimonense on Saturday, with Alejandro Alfaro and Amine Oudrhiri playing just in front of the backline.

Netting the equaliser before the break against Ferencvaros a fortnight ago, it is almost certain that Manuel Pozo is named alongside Dany Jean and Malik Abubakari in the Torreense attack once again this week.

After a fortnight on the sidelines, Ararat-Armenia welcomed midfielder Zidane Banjaqui back to the matchday squad on Sunday, while 34-year-old defender Kamo Hovhannisyan has also returned from injury in the previous week.

Despite playing in the club’s Champions League qualifiers in the summer, Ghanaian forward Paul Ayongo has been left out of the European roster and is the Black and White’s sole miss on Thursday evening.

Having scored five league goals this season, the most of anyone at the club, Arayik Eloyan is likely to be the visitor’s biggest threat in attack this week and will be looking to hit the back of the net for the first time in his career in European competition.

Adriel; David Bruno, Volnei, Stopira, Alcedo; Oudrhiri, Alfaro; Pozo, Jatta, Jean; Abubakari

Joao Bravim; Oliveira, Wilson Valdez, Malis, Grigoryan; Balanta, Carlier; Serobyan, Ambartsumyan, Shaghoyan; Eloyan

Yet to put a point on the board, claiming victory on Thursday’s visit to Portugal looks as though it could be vital for Ararat-Armenia’s chances of potentially progressing to the knockout stages of the Europa League.

However, while they may be struggling domestically, we think Torreense are favourites for victory this week and are backing them to climb out of the elimination places with three points under the lights at the Estadio Dr. Magalhaes Pessoa.

#1761. Arsenal 2-0 Everton: Konsa and Gabriel get the goals

Arsenal made it 7 wins from 8 so far in the Premier League this season with a relatively comfortable 2-0 win over Everton at home yesterday.

Mikel Arteta made some changes from the midweek team, with Ben White, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Mikel Merino, Eberechi Eze and Viktor Gyokeres all handed starts. And as a team that has been a bit slow to get going in games so far, an early goal was just the tonic after all the effort against Bayern Munich on Wednesday.

We put pressure on Everton from the off, with a couple of corners from the Declan Rice side, but another – delivered by Martin Odegaard – drew dividends. Gabriel flicked the ball on, Pickford got a hand to it, it dropped into a dangerous area at the near post and before a defender could get it away, Ezri Konsa was there to poke home from close range to make it 1-0. I quite enjoyed his post-match interview where he spoke about having to wait a long time for his first Arsenal goal, he only joined in the summer and he’s a defender, but I guess you can’t argue against his desire to get off the mark.

After that, Everton enjoyed a little period of the game where they had some possession, but posed little threat, before Arsenal upped the ante and probably should have gone in at half-time further ahead. A lovely move ended with Eze playing a ball into an area where I thought Gyokeres should have attacked it but he was on his heels a bit and it rolled not far wide – maybe Eze could have taken the shot on himself. Rice then fed Noni Madueke who turned well but dragged his shot wide of the far post with his right foot; Merino had an effort blocked; Madueke nearly produced a superb strike with a brilliant touch, turn, and shot from the edge of the box which fizzed just wide of the near post with Pickford rooted to the spot; Odegaard danced through the defence to see a shot deflected wide; and just before half-time Merino flicked a Rice free kick over the bar.

The only thing Everton had to offer was a chance for Thierno Barry when Ben White was unaware of his presence when trying to head back to his goalkeeper, but David Raya was there to make the save. It was pretty much one way traffic, and we absolutely deserved the lead at the break.

In the second half, there was a scare for Gabriel when he landed badly on his knee making a clearance. When he stayed down I thought ‘Oh crap he’s done his hamstring and his ACL and maybe his entire spine and nervous system’. Arsenal seemed to be readying Cristhian Mosquera to come on and replace him, but the Brazilian got some treatment, stretched himself out, and got back on. I was unsure about this, we’ve seen it happen more than once when a player who is hurt compounds the matter by not coming off immediately, but in this case it worked out well because he was the man to double the lead.

The manager had made a triple sub at that point with Kai Havertz, Bruno Guimaraes and Riccardo Calafiori replacing Gyokeres, Merino and Lewis-Skelly (who had been booked), and it was a nice pass from the summer signing to find Ben White’s overlapping run. He stood up a nice cross to the back post and Gabriel was there to head home for 2-0. I was not at all worried about offside despite a VAR check, White timed his run perfectly, you could see that in real-time, and the replays showed that.

Everton did have a decent chance when Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall flashed a header just wide, but really that was about it. There were late cameos for Max Dowman and Martin Zubimendi who took a pointy elbow to the nose and needed treatment for that. Hopefully it doesn’t exclude him from the midweek EFL Cup game, because we need him to be there to start to give Rice a rest.

And that was that. Solid, effective, and with plenty to like about aspects of our performance. Sometimes I feel this Arsenal team can be a bit shot-shy, often looking for the perfect opening before letting fly, and it felt to me like they were instructed to just have a go a bit more yesterday. Merino and Odegaard took five shots each, none of them especially dangerous but it was interesting to note the positions. Four of Odegaard’s were from outside the box, with two of Merino’s from distance (and one from just on the edge). Maybe it’s nothing, just an anomaly, but mixing it up against a team that sat pretty deep is a good idea in my opinion.

We’re very happy with the victory, the performance and the week, because we were given a terrible schedule. Playing Sunday afternoon, then Wednesday night in Munich, coming here really late on Thursday and then having to play again in the Premier League against a really tough opponent on Saturday at 3pm. We have overcome some injuries, and I’m really proud of the mentality of the team in the conditions today.

And paid tribute to his central defensive goalscorers, in particular Konsa who has had a strong start to his Arsenal career:

The two centre-backs scored the goals today. We want to be the best in every phase of play, and we won’t stop until we do it. [Konsa is] unbelievable. To come to a club like Arsenal with no pre-season, Saliba is here and other players, and to position yourself in that manner with the naturality he has and put in the performances he has – the chemistry with Gabi that is so solid – is so difficult to do. We’re lucky to have him.

So a clean sheet, a first half goal, a set-piece goal at long last too, and three points, it’s hard to argue. You can see where we could improve, more efficiency in the final third is going to be an ongoing conversation this season I feel, but I think the manager is right to be proud of his team after a Sunday > Wednesday > Saturday schedule provided a real test – in trying conditions too – and his team came through it very, very well.

There’s a midweek game against Fleetwood to think about next, before what is always a difficult trip to Anfield next weekend. But after that defeat to Brighton, the team has generated some momentum, and let’s hope we can keep that going.

Before I go today, a word of thanks to Andrew and Lewis for keeping things going in my absence, and my apologies that we didn’t have a post-Bayern Arsecast for you. I’d been feeling a bit unwell for a few days, went to A&E to get checked out, and after doing that they decided to keep me in hospital for a bit. Having run a whole loads of tests, and with a need to then wait for results, they let me home on Friday evening. So it’s not a clean bill of health, but they’d done as much as they can at that point.

I just want to say thanks to everyone who was in touch and sent messages/emails – it’s much appreciated. It’s not that you take your health for granted, but when something happens out of the blue it does make you appreciate how life was the day before you found out something wasn’t quite right. I don’t think there’s anything more scary than starting at a white wall in a hospital before they feed you head first into a machine that makes Berlin techno-noises. There’s just too much time to be left alone with your own thoughts, and I don’t like it!

Anyway, we’ll wait and see, and for now things continue as normal. We’ll have an Arsecast Extra for you tomorrow as usual, and in the meantime look after yourselves. Have a great Sunday folks.

#1760. Everyone loves a good comedy

The Premier League continues to amuse this season, with Man Utd’s troubles continuing after a 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth at Old Trafford yesterday. It probably spells the end of Michael Carrick as manager, which is a bit of a shame. I loved his work. Up there with Ruben Amorim and Ruud van Nistelrooy for me. Legend, in my opinion.

Obviously though, United’s problems run deeper than the man on the touchline. The dressing room is a toxic mess, which is quite funny because that’s the kind of thing Sir Jimmy Ratcliffe is an expert in given his position at INEOS – one of the UK’s great polluters. Still, whatever happens at Man Utd, however he continues to ruin internal morale by installing soup kitchens and firing staff like they’re not people worth a moment’s consideration, I guess he can just enjoy life as bigoted old tax-exile in Monaco, wondering why it is that he feels ‘his’ country isn’t what it used to be as he avoids contributing to society by paying his fair share.

I saw a story the other the day in the Athletic about how 72 year old Ratcliffe once went to the physio room to offer players advice on stretching because he’d run the London Marathon. If that doesn’t tell you exactly how dysfunctional that club is, nothing will. Except, of course, for the results on the pitch, the way they play, their position in the table, and the fact that senior players are basically saying ‘F*ck this! I have to go public’ in post-match interviews. But honestly, imagine Stan Kroenke at London Colney giving Viktor Gyokeres advice on how to hold it up, because he’d spent years holding up objections to one of his massively obscene land deals.

I can’t say I have a lot of time for either Lisandro Martinez or Bruno Fernandes, and they will probably become targets for being outspoken. Maybe they were wrong to do it, maybe as captain Fernandes is entirely the wrong kind of character when your club is in this kind of a situation, but it still speaks to the mess that exists on and off the pitch that they’ve said what they’ve said. Yes, it’s very, very entertaining for all of us, but in a purely objective sense, it says a lot.

I remember when Ralf Rangnick was boss there for a while, and he was roundly pilloried because results weren’t good, but he was spot on four or five years ago when he spoke about how the place needed an entire rebuild. I think he said something like it required open heart surgery, and he was absolutely right. All this time later, that operation is still required, but they have a xenophobic egomaniac in charge who would happily deport most of his playing staff if they weren’t talented footballers, and who continues to oversee bad decision after bad decision. Most of the club is still owned by the Glazers who never gave a shit anyway, and as Arsenal fans we know this kind of ownership structure is no good. Now they’ll probably just repeat the cycle where some ex-player will come in on an interim basis, get a few half decent results, and that wobbly-mouthed halfwit Rio Ferdinand will do a giddy dance on live TV about giving him a six year contract because he ‘knows the club’. Which is probably what they’ll do.

Welcome to the hot-seat Darren Fletcher/John O’Shea/Phil Jones/Henning Berg/David May/Alan Smith (the evil blue-lipped one)/Nani. Oh, please, give it to Phil Neville. Listening to Gary tie himself in knots every week on Sky would be amazing. Surely a reward for all us having to listen to him for all these years. Come on universe, you owe us this at least.

I saw a clip of a renowned Man Utd streamer going mad during their humiliating defeat at home yesterday, scornfully saying ‘But it’s Bournemouth! It’s Bournemouth!’, which tells you plenty. Anyone who has watched Bournemouth over the last few seasons would understand that even with a new manager in charge, they are a really good side with good players who can hurt you. The arrogance, the hubris, to think that just because their ground only holds a fraction of the capacity of Ancient Trafford, you are entitled to win the game.

I’m not saying he is part of the problem, per se, but if that level of delusion exists within their fanbase despite all the evidence they’ve had presented to them – right in front of their very eyes! – then it probably tells you something about the job that club needs to do. Thankfully for all of us, they appear to have a collection of people in charge thoroughly incapable of doing that. Sir Jimmy might brilliant at pumping petrochemical run-off into the atmosphere and poisoning wildlife, but he seems to be something of a footballing idiot. And quite hilariously, their current chief executive is a man called Omar Berrada, who used to work at Man City where two of his job titles between 2011 and 2015 were ‘Head of International Business Development’ and ‘Director of Partnership Sales’. What an interesting timeline that is, eh?!

I know we all have our issues with Arsenal, and we’ve been through some stuff over the years, but on this Monday morning as we begin a new week, let’s take a moment to be thankful for where we are right now. One decision can absolutely change the trajectory of your football club, and for us that was the appointment of Mikel Arteta. Reading lately that other options were considered ahead of him gave me a shudder, because we absolutely would not be in the same rude health if we’d gone down those particularly avenues.

Which is to say, the very best of luck to the Steve Bruce – Gary Pallister dream team.

Right, I’ll leave it there for now, but we will have an Arsecast Extra for you a bit later on today. We’ve already put out the call for questions on BlueSky @gunnerblog.bsky.social and @arseblog.com, so fire away using the hashtag #arsecastextra – or if you’re an Arseblog Member on Patreon, leave your question in the #arsecast-extra-questions channel on our Discord server.

The pod should be out around around noon or so. Until then, have a good one.

#1756. AZ Alkmaar vs Juventus - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 03 Nov 2026 16:54, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 16:58

One point apart in the Europa League table, Juventus and AZ Alkmaar are both vying for automatic qualification to this season's last 16.

Set to meet at AFAS Stadion on Thursday evening, Juve have started strongly, but AZ boast a long unbeaten home record in UEFA competition.

More accustomed to dining at Europe's top table, Juventus started their Europa League campaign with a 5-0 cruise at home to NEC, before being made to work much harder for victory over Celta Vigo on matchday two.

Nick Woltemade and Randal Kolo Muani both scored as Juve beat Celta and moved top of the table, but they slipped down to seventh with a home draw last time out.

After Zeki Celik had opened the scoring against Rennes, the hosts then found themselves 2-1 down heading into the final half-hour, before Woltemade equalised from the spot.

Since then, it has been quite a mixed bag in Serie A, as the Bianconeri beat Lecce 2-0, then lost to Genoa by the same scoreline, setting up a tense clash with Napoli on Sunday night.

Ahead of kickoff in Turin, Luciano Spalletti's injury-hit side lay 11 points behind the league leaders, below newly promoted Frosinone and just above city rivals Torino.

With his job potentially on the line, Spalletti really had to beat a club he memorably led to the Scudetto in 2023, and stunning strikes from Kerim Alajbegovic and Jeremie Boga eventually got the job done.

In contrast to their domestic woes, Juventus have lost just one of their last 10 continental games, while scoring at least twice in eight - so they may welcome a return to the Europa League.

Heading into the clubs' first competitive meeting, Juve are seventh in the table on seven points, while AZ sit one point behind in 10th place.

The Dutch side have responded well after an opening-day defeat to Sunderland, first beating Hapoel Be'er Sheva on home turf, then strolling to victory in Yerevan.

AZ simply swept Ararat-Armenia aside at the end of last month, with Brazilian winger Weslley Patati scoring twice in an emphatic 4-0 win.

Now heading back to Alkmaar, they have won 14 and lost none of their last 17 European home matches, dating back to a Conference League clash with Aston Villa three years ago.

However, like Juve, they have recently been below par on the domestic scene: Leeroy Echteld's side have only taken one point from their last four league games, leaving them fifth in the Eredivisie.

Amid a tough run of fixtures, they lost 2-0 at Feyenoord, drew 2-2 with Cambuur and were beaten 2-0 at home by Twente, before losing 1-0 to Ajax in Amsterdam.

Juventus are still missing several men, as their relentless injury crisis continues.

Celik and Nico Gonzalez most recently joined Kenan Yildiz, Khephren Thuram, Francisco Conceicao, Kamil Grabara and captain Manuel Locatelli on the sidelines.

Furthermore, Weston McKennie, Juan Cabal and Alajbegovic all sustained knocks against Napoli, though they are expected to play some part in Alkmaar.

With Jeff Ekhator just returning, there are few alternatives to Kolo Muani and Woltemade, the latter of whom is joint-top scorer in this season's Europa League with three goals.

AZ forwards Patati and Mexx Meerdink have notched two apiece, and they are likely to feature in the hosts' front three.

Ayoub Oufkir is another option, as he returns from a domestic suspension, while rising star Kees Smit should be back on the bench after recovering from injury.

Club captain Peer Koopmeiners could come up against his big brother Teun, who scored 35 times in 116 AZ appearances and may play for Juve in midfield.

De Busser; Dijkstra, Goes, Hoedt, De Wit; Kwakman, P. Koopmeiners; Patati, Stengs, Daal; Meerdink

Vicario; Kalulu, Gatti, Bremer, Cambiaso; Luiz, Sarr; Kolo Muani, T. Koopmeiners, Alajbegovic; Woltemade

They may have made minimal progress in Serie A since Spalletti arrived one year ago, but Juventus are still a force at Europa League level.

With a little luck, the Bianconeri could even threaten AZ's long unbeaten streak on home turf, but the spoils will most likely be shared.

#1755. A chance for rotation and rest as we face Fleetwood Town

We’re in EFL Cup action this evening, taking on Fleetwood Town at Highbury Stadium (not that one). Tonight’s opposition sit 18th in League Two, and this will surely influence Mikel Arteta’s team selection. There are players I just do not want to see this evening. Not just from the start, but not in the squad at all.

The likes of Declan Rice, Gabriel, Ezri Konsa, Martin Odegaard have all played a lot and could use a night off, and I would also include the two wide players we have fit – Noni Madueke and Eberechi Eze. With injuries to Bukayo Saka and Christos Tzolis, we’re very light in that area of the pitch, and we do not need to risk them in a game like this. There’s still plenty of scope for rotation, and there are some senior players who could use some minutes, as well as an opportunity to fill out the bench with Academy lads.

You imagine we’ll see starts for Kepa, Martin Zubimendi (assuming his nose isn’t too sore after the weekend), Cristhian Mosquera, Piero Hincapie, Mikel Merino, maybe Jurrien Timber, Myles Lewis-Skelly, and possibly Bruno Guimaraes, but also it’s an opportunity for Marli Salmon and Max Dowman again, both of whom started in the last round against Ipswich. Dowman played centrally that evening, in the Odegaard role, and got two goals, but I wonder if tonight he might be used out wide as we rest Madueke.

After that, young players like Ife Ibrahim and Theo Julienne will be hoping for minutes to add to the ones they picked up in the last round, while forwards like Ceadach O’Neill and Igor Tyjon might fancy their chances of being included. This is a kind draw ahead of a weekend trip to Anfield, and with Liverpool playing Chelsea tomorrow night, it’s an opportunity for the manager to ease the burden on the guys who have played a lot as well as giving the next generation a chance too.

I think we’ll also see Viktor Gyokeres up front, and the Swedish international could really do with a goal. He’s on a barren streak (in club terms at least), that stretches back to May 2nd, and it’s now 15 games without a goal. Even though his minutes have been a bit scant this season, that’s a record that’s hanging over him and one he’ll want to put right. A goal, or goals, against a League Two side in this competition will always have that little caveat applied, but it ought to be a real opportunity for him to build a little goalscoring confidence, so fingers crossed he can do exactly that.

Speaking about tonight’s game, Arteta said:

Every time you play a football match, and especially against a team in a different division, respect the game, respect every opponent because they deserve to do that, and then try to win and try to play better than them.

So, let’s see how it plays out later on, kick off is 20.00 in this part of the world.

Elsewhere, while I find the concept of individual awards in football completely counter-intuitive to what makes the game as compelling as it is, I did want to mention Bukayo Saka winning the Socrates Award at the Ballon d’Or ceremony last night. The official website reports that: “Bukayo and his family have worked with multiple charities, including long-term projects with Big Shoe, providing medical care and humanitarian aid for children and families in need in London and around the world.”

And yet, they are often held up as an example of people who earn too much for doing too little. I remember during Covid, politicians singled out football players as those who should set an example by taking wage cuts or making charity donations or supporting the health services, while ignoring those who – less publicly – earn far, far more. But as we can see here, someone like Bukayo Saka (and he’s far from alone too), uses what his talent has provided to help others, and while I’m sure he doesn’t do it for awards or recognition, this spotlight on what he does can help the causes he supports.

This is an individual award worth highlighting, and you can see the ceremony and his speech about it below.

Right, I’m gonna leave it there for now. As ever, we’ll bring you live blog coverage of the game later, as well all the post-game stuff on Arseblog News like the match report, player ratings, manager reaction, quotes round-up and more. Don’t forget the updated Arseblog apps also have a cool new matchday centre, full of stats, alerts, and much more.

The Arsecast Extra is below too if you haven’t had a chance to listen yet. Catch you later for the game.

#1751. Fleetwood Town 1-1 Arsenal (5-3 pens): A dismal night at Highbury

Arsenal crashed out of the Carabao Cup last night, going down 5-3 on penalties to Fleetwood Town after a 1-1 draw in normal time.

Mikel Arteta made changes, as you’d expect, with starts for young players Marli Salmon, Max Dowman and Ceadach O’Neill, while thus far peripheral senior men like Martin Zubimendi, Cristhian Mosquera and Piero Hincapie also came in for what ought to have been valuable playing time. He also decided, somewhat curiously in my opinion, to start both of his strikers, with Viktor Gyokeres up front and Kai Havertz behind him in midfield.

There was a surreal start to the game when the referee spotted a drone hovering above Highbury Stadium and stopped play. I’m unsure what the big issue was however. Was he worried about player safety, TV rights? Whatever it was, we were stalled for 8 minutes until it was sorted out, not ideal for both sets of players on a night when conditions weren’t exactly clement.

When play began again Arsenal dominated the ball but struggled to test the home side. Hincapie headed a Dowman cross over, before the 16 year old had a clear sight of goal but scuffed his right-footed shot wide. In the middle, Gyokeres looked unhappy as if the ball should have been squared but the shot was the right decision, the execution of it was the issue.

Then, Fleetwood scored. We weren’t competitive enough around the second ball after a long kick from the goalkeeper, they played it forward, and Aaron Loupalo-Bi got the wrong side of Salmon before firing home through the legs of Illan Meslier. It’s not great defending from the 17 year old, but it’s one of those moments as a young player that are inevitable and that ultimately you learn from. He was superb against Ipswich in the last round, and given how badly we fared further forward with more experienced players, I don’t think we should give this much more than a passing mention.

Decent balls in from Dowman gave Havertz and Timber headed chances which they spurned before the break, and that was the extent of our attacking play in that first period. So, it was no surprise when the manager made changes at the break with Ben White and Martin Odegaard replacing Salmon and Timber. It meant a bit of a reshuffle, and early in the second half we found an equaliser.

O’Neill, who looked lively on the left, played a decent ball in from that side, Fleetwood’s defenders didn’t deal with it, Gyokeres – as he does too often – fell over, but on his way down touched it beyond the keeper for 1-1. And that should have been the point at which the game changed in our favour, but what we produced subsequent to the goal was just dismal. Odegaard made us a little bit better, but around him few others stepped up.

Havertz was abysmal missing a great chance after Odegaard’s clever pass put him through, and Gyokeres completing 5 of 9 passes all night against League Two opposition illustrates the limitations of his game in stark fashion. When we need a focal point up front, he just cannot provide it. Eberechi Eze came on and made little difference, and while perhaps there’s some mitigation for Martin Zubimendi playing with a broken nose, he completely failed to impose himself on the game in any meaningful way for a player of his calibre. And then everything was compounded by the red card.

After a bit of a scramble near the touchline there was a strong tackle on Dowman, one which took ball but also slid through on the man. He took exception to it, there was a very slight retaliatory movement with his leg which sparked a bit of a melee (Ben White was right on the scene to protect his teammate), and the referee adjudged it sufficient to send Dowman off. I think it’s very, very harsh.

I don’t think the challenge from the Fleetwood player is quite as bad as some make out, but I can understand why Max reacted. He shouldn’t have done that, but you can’t send a player off for that. It wasn’t a kick, it wasn’t violent conduct, and I think an experienced referee should have been able to sort that out with a couple of yellow cards. Whether Arsenal will appeal the severity of a three match ban remains to be seen, but I think they have a good case to do so if they choose.

What I really didn’t like, however, was Arteta’s reaction as Dowman went off. He clearly gave him an earful, and said afterwards, “Something that we discussed already before the match.”

A little earlier there had been a confrontation between Odegaard and a Fleetwood player, and I think we can all understand the manager warning his players not to rise to any kind of bait. Nevertheless, Max Dowman is 16, and the manager’s job is to protect him. It doesn’t mean he has to be mollycoddled, it doesn’t mean he shouldn’t face the internal consequences of being shown a red card, but that should have played out in the dressing room, not on the touchline and on live TV. Arteta has done incredible work at this football club, but he’s not infallible, and in my opinion he got this one really wrong – regardless of how frustrated he might be with the reaction from Dowman.

There was a late flurry from Arsenal as we looked to avoid penalties. The keeper made a very good save from Ben White, Odegaard had a shot which required another stop, and just before the end there was a really presentable chance for Havertz from an Eze cross which he headed tamely wide with no conviction. A moment which summed his own performance, and that of the team. Feeble.

So then penalties. Fleetwood made no mistake with five solid spot kicks, we made one through Bruno Guimaraes, and that was that. A massive win for the home side, and fair play to them for it. It’s a night that will live long in the history of that club, and this is what cup football can throw up. It’s not the first time we’ve been the giant killed by a lower league side, but I really don’t think we can have any complaints because of how poorly we played overall. Congrats to them.

First of all, congratulations to Fleetwood for going through the next round. The manner that they have done it, and for us a very sad day. There is nothing to criticise the players for their attitude, their application. The determination – you could see that was there from the start.

The team keeps trying and trying with the ball with chances, shots and especially shots that we had not to score many more goals. Then you don’t capitalise, then you cannot go through to the next round. Unfortunately, we are out.

I will say I think that’s a very generous assessment of our performance. Protective almost, in a way the comments about Dowman were not. There’s a big difference between having a lot of the ball and making that possession count, and while nights like this can happen, upsets are part of football, too many players out there last night let themselves down. Ahead of a big game at Anfield at the weekend, it’s not ideal, because some of them are going to have to play, and if they’re anything like they were last night, we’ll be in trouble. If you already harbour some concerns about our attacking potency, last night will done nothing to assuage them.

I can’t sit here this morning and say I’m devastated at going out of this competition, but this was a night which produced many more questions than answers. If you were generous you’d say we were rusty and the changed nature of the side meant we lacked cohesion. The other assessment might be that we were absolutely terrible on the night, and even if some players are trying to find some rhythm and match sharpness, we ought to have produced a lot better than that embarrassing load of shit. I tend to connect far more with the latter than the former.

Any defeat at Arsenal creates fallout. That’s something we’re going to have to contend with ahead of the weekend, and the lack of a post-game press conference means legitimate questions about the performance, some individuals, and the manager’s reaction to the sending off will have to wait until Friday, so this is gonna linger like an eggy fart in lift for a few days more.

Update: Seems there was some post-game stuff.

Right, I’ll leave it there for morning. Have a good one folks.

#1750. GdS: How Amorim’s fluidity helped Rabiot record career-best start to a season

Adrien Rabiot continues to deliver in the biggest games for AC Milan, and Ruben Amorim is arguably getting the best ever form out of him.

La Gazzetta dello Sport begin a report by recalling how different things were in the summer. With Milan falling to fifth and Massmiliano Allegri being sacked, many presumed that Rabiot could follow him to Napoli, to play Champions League football.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Rabiot not only remained at Milanello, but is also the Atlas of the team this year. He carries it on his shoulders and takes its weight with disarming ease and personality. While Allegri observes Milan from below, Adrien has found a new coach who is giving him a new lease of life.

The derby goal is an excellent indicator of Rabiot’s confidence, attempting that billiard-like shot (even though some, like Yunus Musah, maintain it was a cross) in a match like this, with the game still wide open, signifies complete self-confidence.

The Frenchman knows perfectly well he has a powerful shot, but he opted for finesse, guiding the ball to kiss the post and land in the back of the net as eleven Nerazzurri players watched it slowly and mockingly cross their penalty area.

Rabiot was one of the derby’s heroes but has been performing at a high level for several matches now. He currently has the best average rating in the squad, and it’s a stratospheric 6.81 (out of 10, across all games).

The other key number is nine: five goals and four assists this season makes nine contributions, the most in the squad. In the league, he’s been involved in a goal in each of his last five games: assists against Lazio, goals against Lecce and Sassuolo, a goal and assist against Atalanta, and a goal in the derby.

To better understand his further improvement from an already very high level, we must consider that in the entire last season, Adrien had six goals and four assists. He’s one goal away from matching that tally.

Some tactical considerations help contextualise things. Compared to Allegri, Amorim’s style of football is on another level, being much more attacking. It’s not based solely on counter-attacks, but on a flow of play that starts from midfield and allows for the runs of those who move in between the lines.

Rabiot has always been a player who can get forward: he has the physique, technique, and footballing intelligence. Amorim has given him a further step because he’s made him more difficult to read for opponents.

If before, the Frenchman was a classic pivot midfielder, now you find him practically everywhere. At the start of the season, Amorim’s style of football was positional, locked into a 3-4-2-1 that seemed set in stone with Rabiot behind the striker.

Then the Portuguese coach realised he was doing himself harm and began a tactical overhaul. The fundamentalist has become fluid, and the playing system is now an abstract concept that must be filled with individual interpretations.

This is a set of circumstances where Rabiot shines. The derby is a perfect example: the former PSG man was everywhere, depending on his own tendencies and the team’s need for certain characteristics in certain parts if the pitch.

This is the best start to a season of his career. Now, in addition to the pitch, he’ll also have to keep an eye on his desk. After Strahinja Pavlovic and Christian Pulisic, he’s the next one destined to ascend to the fourth floor of Casa Milan to sign a renewal waiting for him.
